nodes.title: Dogfood mgit on its own repo (adopt mgit for mgit-dev development)
nodes.prompt:
DOGFOODING INITIATIVE (owner-directed, 2026-06-23). The mgit-dev repo's own development has been PURE GIT the whole time — there is no .mgit store. "If we don't use mgit, why would the world?" Adopt mgit for mgit's own development so the team feels the product under real (incl. parallel-agent) load and the friction becomes the backlog. Do this DELIBERATELY (not bolted onto feature-delivery under risk).

WHY IT MATTERS: the canonical mgit scenario — an LLM agent doing task-tagged work, spawning parallel sub-agents in isolated worktrees — is exactly what we DON'T do on our own repo (we reach for git because it's the path of least resistance). That is the strongest possible adoption-warning signal; closing it both validates and hardens the product.

FRICTION / PUNCH-LIST found today (2026-06-23) trying to switch parallel build-agents to mgit worktrees:
1. Not initialized: no .mgit store in the repo; `mgit worktree add` is unusable until `mgit init` + the current tree is imported (worktrees materialize from .mgit, which starts empty — an un-imported worktree has no source to build).
2. init UX bug: a STALE mgit binary's `mgit init` printed usage + rc=1 (looked like a no-op) but actually CREATED a half-baked .mgit dir; the resulting store had NO valid HEAD (`mgit log`/`mgit status` → "reference not found"). init should be atomic — fail cleanly OR leave a valid initial HEAD; never a corrupt HEAD-less store. (Also: a stale binary gave a misleading error; consider a version/repo-format check.)
3. Bootstrap cost: adopting on an existing repo with history needs importing the entire working tree into .mgit (mgit add + commit) + base/task branch setup — make this a one-command path (e.g. `mgit init --import` / `mgit adopt`).
4. mgit→git integration loop UNPROVEN for the agent workflow: agent `mgit commit` in a worktree → `mgit squash --to-git` → git main → push. Validate end-to-end (this is the loop that lets mgit-tracked work reach the GitHub git remote).
5. Agent-harness can't natively isolate into an mgit worktree: Claude Code's Agent tool only does GIT worktrees (`isolation: worktree`); running an agent in an mgit worktree requires manual `mgit worktree add` + cwd plumbing the harness doesn't support. This is an adoption blocker for the seamless-agent story — relates to MGIT-11.11 (agent integration) and the `mgit run` hook surface.

ACCEPTANCE: mgit-dev development runs ON mgit — repo mgit-init'd (coexisting with git, project .git provably untouched, MGIT-14), current tree imported, task branches via mgit, parallel build-agents run in mgit worktrees, and their work lands to git main via a validated mgit→git path; the init UX (item 2) and the import/integration loop (3,4) are fixed/validated; the harness↔mgit-worktree friction (5) is documented and a path proposed. No co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer.
nodes.acceptance: mgit-dev development runs on mgit (init'd over git with .git untouched, tree imported, task branches via mgit, parallel agents in mgit worktrees, work lands to git main via a validated mgit->git loop); the init-UX corruption bug is fixed; a one-command adopt/import path exists; and the agent-harness <-> mgit-worktree isolation friction is documented with a proposed path.

nodes.title: macOS containment profiles: default vzf+Linux guest, opt-in mac-native (workload-selected)
nodes.prompt:
PRODUCT DECISION (owner, 2026-06-24): macOS sandboxing offers a per-task CONTAINMENT PROFILE. DEFAULT = vzf + Linux guest (the current backend — right for agents whose workload targets Linux/cross-platform: web, backend, Go/Node servers). OPT-IN = mac-native, for mac-native workloads (Swift/Xcode, mac-only libs/frameworks, brew) that CANNOT run in a Linux guest. The user's agent CHOOSES the profile based on its workload.

WHY: a Linux microVM can't run a macOS-native toolchain — `xcodebuild`/`swift build`/`pod install`/mac-only native bindings fail or are meaningless in a Linux guest. So mac-native dev needs a different containment environment than the Linux microVM. (Clarified that the "Linux VM" was an FR-17/ADR-005 IMPLEMENTATION choice, not the core requirement, which is CONTAINMENT.)

SCOPE / OPEN DESIGN:
1. Containment-profile selection in the launch path: a per-task profile {vzf-linux (default), mac-native}, chosen by the agent/policy from the workload (analogous to network mode). Composes with the existing build-tagged backend selection (cmd/mgit-sandboxd/platform_backend*.go + sandboxd.SelectBackend). The agent-integration hooks (MGIT-11.11 / `mgit run`) surface the choice.
2. The mac-native backend — DESIGN DECISION REQUIRED, with real tradeoffs:
   - macOS GUEST VM under Virtualization.framework: true VM isolation + mac libs, but heavy (full macOS image GBs, slow boot, Apple's 2-VM-per-host limit, a whole macOS guest stack — a macOS analog of mgit-guest + the exec/land/notify transport). Strongest isolation; biggest lift.
   - Host-level App Sandbox / sandbox-exec: light + mac-native, but PROCESS confinement, not a VM — does NOT give the "blast radius = a disposable VM" guarantee the README leads with; sandbox-exec is deprecated; App Sandbox needs entitlements. Weaker isolation.
   - (macOS 15+ Containerization.framework runs LINUX containers — same Linux-guest limitation, does not solve mac-native.)
   Pick the model (or support both with a documented isolation-strength tradeoff), preserving SEC-03/SEC-04-equivalent guarantees where the model allows; where it can't (host sandbox), document the reduced-isolation posture explicitly (like the container fallback).
3. SEC-03 quarantine, egress enforcement, verified land, and the README's containment claim must each be reconciled per profile — a host App-Sandbox can't give microVM-grade guarantees; be honest about what each profile delivers.

Refs: ADR-005, FR-17, README containment positioning. No co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer.
nodes.acceptance: A per-task macOS containment profile exists (default vzf+Linux guest; opt-in mac-native), selectable by the agent/policy from the workload; the mac-native backend is designed+built per a recorded model decision (macOS guest VM vs host sandbox) with its isolation guarantees documented honestly per profile; selection composes with the existing backend wiring; the containment claims (SEC-03/SEC-04/land) are reconciled and documented per profile.

nodes.title: Dogfood head-to-head: mgit sandbox + micro-commit substrate vs plain devcontainer/git — is the marginal value real?
nodes.prompt:
USEFULNESS VALIDATION (owner-requested, 2026-06-24; tabled to do AFTER finishing the current feature work). Stop building mgit's value on faith; run the cheapest test that proves or kills it.

TWO things to validate head-to-head, on a real throwaway coding-agent task (e.g. add a small feature that does `npm install`/`pip install`):

A. CONTAINMENT (FR-17 sandbox) vs a plain devcontainer/`docker run`: run the SAME agent session inside mgit's microVM sandbox and inside a plain container. The only question that matters: what did mgit's sandbox STOP or GUARANTEE that the container didn't (default-deny egress, no repo-history leak into the guest per SEC-03, attested one-way task-scoped land-back), and was it worth the extra setup? Use the existing x86_64 KVM box — no arm64 detour needed.

B. MICRO-COMMIT SUBSTRATE (part 1) vs git-with-a-scratch-branch-convention: does an agent (and a review-agent/user) ACTUALLY exercise the load-bearing capability — backtrack to an earlier micro-commit, fork, preserve the old line, proceed, and cherry-pick the good bits — or does it just fix-forward / redo-in-place, leaving the micro-commits as squashed-away scaffolding nobody climbs? If the backtrack/fork/cherry-pick loop isn't exercised, the micro-granularity is busywork and the moat collapses to "git with a constrained agent UX."

DELIVERABLE: a brutally honest written verdict per A and B — "kept the value" or "a plain container/git was fine." If A holds → strip the safety-critical VCS framing, lead purely on containment + clean land-back. If B holds → backtrack/fork/cherry-pick is the headline; make it dead-simple for agents. If either fails → that's the most valuable + cheapest thing to learn before building MGIT-27 and further epics.

No co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer in any commit. LAN IP stays out of git.
nodes.acceptance: A real agent task is run inside mgit's sandbox AND a plain container, and inside mgit micro-commits AND plain git scratch-branch; a written verdict states, per A (containment) and B (micro-commit backtrack/fork/cherry-pick), what mgit guaranteed/enabled that the alternative did not and whether it was worth the cost; a recommendation follows (lead on containment / lead on backtrack-fork / pivot) grounded in what was actually observed, not asserted.

nodes.title: Reframe docs + author agent skills: position mgit as the safe, checkpointed working substrate for HyperSwe coding agents (drop DO-178C pitch)
nodes.prompt:
PURPOSE: Make mgit sell itself to a developer (README) AND make LLM agents reliably follow mgit's engineering discipline (skills). This is not docs polish — the skills are the MECHANISM that realizes mgit's core value. Owner's thesis (2026-06-24): agents are AI; given clear, noise-free, step-by-step instructions, they WILL follow the micro-commit / backtrack / fork / cherry-pick discipline, and THAT is when mgit shows its true value. So author the skills with that weight.

=== FULL CONTEXT (read before touching anything) ===
mgit is part of the HyperSwe product suite, where coding agents develop features. mgit has TWO unified pillars that together = "let an agent build a feature safely, then land only the reviewed result":

PILLAR 1 — CONTAINMENT (FR-17 sandbox): the agent's untrusted code (npm/pip installs, builds, tests) runs in a disposable per-task microVM, not on the user's machine; default-deny egress; only verified, task-tagged changes land back. Blast radius of a poisoned dependency = a throwaway VM, not the user's SSH keys / cloud creds / disk. (README already leads with this — REFINE, don't rewrite.)

PILLAR 2 — CHECKPOINTED WORKING SUBSTRATE (the VCS): instead of crowding the user's real git repo with agent micro-commit noise, the agent micro-commits every small, coherent step into an isolated `.mgit` store (go-git, provably never touches the project `.git` — see MGIT-14). On review (by the user OR a review-agent), if a decision turns out wrong (e.g. a bad library choice), you BACKTRACK to the exact micro-commit, FORK from there (preserving the old line), proceed with the new approach, and CHERRY-PICK the useful bits from the old branch — course-correct instead of throw-away-and-redo. `squash` collapses the micro-commits for the land. So micro-granularity's value is IN-TASK (course correction) + review granularity; the landed artifact is squashed.

POSITIONING SHIFT (the core of this ticket): DROP the "safety-critical VCS for avionics/medical/defense (DO-178C / IEC 62304 / NASA-STD-8739.8 / MIL-STD-498)" framing as the product's reason-to-exist and headline pitch. There is no such customer; it is aspirational marketing that makes mgit heavier and harder to adopt, and we don't even use it ourselves. KEEP the genuine engineering discipline (TDD, append-only audit, parameterized SQL, go-git determinism, coverage bars, function/file limits) as HOW mgit is built and as the discipline agents follow — just stop selling mgit AS a safety-critical-compliance product. The honest pitch is: "the safe, checkpointed working substrate for HyperSwe coding agents."

HONEST CAVEATS that the docs MUST respect (do not overclaim):
- mgit is git underneath (go-git). The moat is the agent-UX/discipline + sandbox-land integration, NOT storage tech. The honest alternative a skeptical dev compares against is "git + a scratch-branch convention." Sell the workflow + integration, not novel storage.
- The load-bearing backtrack/fork/cherry-pick loop is UNPROVEN (agents today default to fix-forward/redo-in-place). MGIT-28 is the tabled head-to-head test of exactly this. So docs must claim "mgit makes course-correction cheap AND the skill instructs the agent to use it" — NOT "agents reliably backtrack" (unproven). The most believable actor is the REVIEWER directing the backtrack; design skills for BOTH autonomous-agent and reviewer-directed use.
- macOS reality (see MGIT-27): default macOS profile = vzf + LINUX guest (right for Linux/cross-platform workloads); opt-in mac-native profile for mac-native workloads (Swift/Xcode/brew) is a FUTURE capability the agent selects by workload. README must NOT claim seamless macOS-native containment; state the Linux-guest default + the mac-native option honestly. The "hardware-isolated VM" is the mechanism (an implementation choice), the requirement is CONTAINMENT.

VERIFIED FACTS: all needed CLI commands EXIST in cmd/mgit/ — `commit`, `log`, `status`, `diff`, `show`, `branch`, `checkout`, `cherry-pick`, `rollback`, `restore`, `squash`, `merge`, `worktree`, `run`, `sandbox` (launch/exec/land/grant/connect/image), `verify`, `audit`. The skill must map the discipline to these REAL commands; verify exact flags via `--help`/the command's cobra definition before writing examples. Do NOT instruct agents to use a flag/command that doesn't exist.

=== DELIVERABLES (exact files + how to modify) ===

1. README.md (root) — the developer sell. It already leads with containment (keep that). Changes:
   a. Add a one-line "Part of the HyperSwe suite" context near the top.
   b. Rewrite the "second pillar" section (currently "surgical rollback / append-only audit trail") into the full CHECKPOINTED WORKING SUBSTRATE story: isolated `.mgit` (never pollutes your real git, MGIT-14) → agent micro-commits each step → backtrack to a decision point → fork & continue (preserve the old line) → cherry-pick the good bits → squash → land only the reviewed result. Use the ascii flow already present as a base but extend it to fork+cherry-pick, not just rollback.
   c. Add a concrete "How an agent works a task with mgit" walkthrough (a real command sequence: `mgit run -- <agent>` → micro `mgit commit`s → review with `mgit log`/`mgit diff` → `mgit rollback`/`mgit checkout -b` fork → `mgit cherry-pick` → `mgit squash` → land) so a dev SEES the workflow value.
   d. Fix the macOS framing per MGIT-27 (default vzf+Linux guest; mac-native is a planned opt-in profile) — remove any implication of seamless macOS-native execution.
   e. Audit for and remove residual safety-critical/DO-178C MARKETING as headline value (reframe "append-only audit trail" into the user-facing "you can always see and undo exactly what the agent did"). Keep the honest security-posture caveat block (already present, good).
   f. Honest claims only (respect the caveats above).

2. internal/agentadapter/claudemd.go (RenderClaudeMdSection) + claudemd_test.go — THE primary agent skill surface (this block is injected into every sandboxed agent's CLAUDE.md). Today it only covers the sandbox env + network. ADD a clear, noise-free, IMPERATIVE "mgit working discipline" subsection inside the marked block instructing the agent to: commit a small task-tagged micro-commit after each coherent step (cheap + expected; they get squashed at land, so don't hesitate); use `mgit log`/`mgit status`/`mgit diff` to orient; when a prior decision proves wrong, `mgit rollback`/`mgit checkout` to that point and fork rather than rewrite from scratch; `mgit cherry-pick` salvage from the old line; the operator/review-agent may direct these. Keep it MINIMAL and noise-free (owner explicitly wants signal, not prose). MUST stay secret-free (read only SandboxEnv, no ambient state) and idempotent (within the existing BEGIN/END markers). Update RenderClaudeMdSection tests to assert the new discipline lines + continued secret-freedom.

3. A dedicated, noise-free mgit AGENT SKILL doc (the "robust skills" the owner asked for). Decide the right home (a skill file shipped/installed alongside the agent adapters or `mgit run`, consistent with how `.mtix/docs/SKILL.md` / `mtix plugin install` ship skills). It must give step-by-step, low-noise instructions for the FULL discipline: task pickup → micro-commit cadence → checkpoint → backtrack → fork → cherry-pick → review handoff → squash → land, each with a real command example (verified against the CLI). Written for BOTH an autonomous agent and a reviewer directing course-correction. Imperative, minimal, copy-pasteable.

4. .mtix/docs/SKILL.md — drop the "Safety-critical operating procedures are baked in" line and the "Compliance References (do-178c/iec-62304/nasa/mil-std checklists)" section as the headline; reframe around the real engineering discipline + the mgit working-substrate workflow. Keep the genuinely useful task-discipline rules (context-chain traversal, no-code-without-a-task, no-stub, completeness test).

5. CLAUDE.md (root, contributor directives) — surgically reframe ONLY the TITLE+ROLE STATEMENT and "Design Context" sections: mgit = the safe, checkpointed working substrate + containment for HyperSwe coding agents; remove the avionics/medical/defense customer framing and the "safety-critical micro version control system" headline. KEEP intact ALL the real engineering rules below it (TDD workflow, SQL laws, go-git rules, coverage table, function/file limits, security mindset) — those are valuable and stay. This is a reframe of the framing, NOT a gutting of the discipline. If you prefer, retain a single honest line like "built to a high-integrity bar" but not as the raison d'être.

=== CONSTRAINTS ===
- Honest claims only; never assert value MGIT-28 hasn't validated. Cross-reference MGIT-27 (macOS profiles) and MGIT-28 (head-to-head validation) where relevant.
- The injected CLAUDE.md block must remain secret-free + idempotent; tests must prove it.
- Verify every referenced command/flag exists before documenting it; if the discipline needs a capability the CLI lacks, FILE a follow-up task — do not document a fake command.
- No co-authored-by / agent / "Generated with" trailer in any commit. No LAN IP in any doc or commit (refer to "the KVM box"/"Linux runner").
- Run the full gate before done: build (darwin+linux), test, -race, vet, golangci-lint (0 across all build tags), anti-stub grep.

Consider decomposing into per-deliverable children (README; injected-claudemd skill; standalone agent skill; .mtix SKILL.md; root CLAUDE.md reframe) — each is independently shippable.
nodes.acceptance: README sells the unified two-pillar story (containment + checkpointed working substrate) honestly, with the HyperSwe context, a concrete agent-task walkthrough using real commands, the accurate macOS profile reality (MGIT-27), and no safety-critical/DO-178C customer framing as headline value. A dedicated, noise-free mgit agent skill exists covering the full micro-commit→backtrack→fork→cherry-pick→squash→land discipline (autonomous + reviewer-directed) using only verified commands. internal/agentadapter/claudemd.go injects that discipline into every sandboxed agent's CLAUDE.md, secret-free + idempotent, with passing tests. .mtix/docs/SKILL.md and the root CLAUDE.md TITLE/Design-Context are reframed off the DO-178C-customer framing while preserving all genuine engineering discipline. Every documented command/flag verified to exist (gaps filed, not faked). No overclaim beyond what is built/validated; MGIT-28 referenced as the pending value test. Full gate green; no banned commit trailers; no LAN IP in docs.

nodes.title: Service Layer
nodes.description: Business logic: commit, squash, rollback, branch, diff, verify, audit, config services.
nodes.prompt:
CONTEXT: Service Layer — Waves 5-6

You are building the business logic layer for mgit. Services sit between the store layer (go-git + SQLite) and the presentation layers (CLI, REST API, MCP). ALL business logic lives here — handlers never access stores directly.

ARCHITECTURE:
  internal/service/commit.go — CommitService: CreateCommit (FR-2, FR-3). Accepts task_id, agent_id, session_id, file_diffs, message. Computes tree_hash via TreeStore.BuildTree(). Generates SHA-256 content_hash. Stores in both go-git (CommitStore) and SQLite (IndexStore). Auto-generates messages if not provided.
  internal/service/squash.go — SquashService: SquashTask (FR-7). Retrieves all commits for task, verifies chain integrity, merges FileDiffs into single diff, creates squashed commit atomically. Optional --to-git export. ALL-OR-NOTHING: if any step fails, entire operation rolls back.

nodes.title: mgit add/status should honor .gitignore (first dogfood finding on mgit-dev)
nodes.prompt:
FIRST DOGFOOD FINDING (2026-06-26, MGIT-26 pilot): after `mgit init` on the real mgit-dev repo, both `mgit add .` and `mgit status` IGNORE the repo's .gitignore. Observed:
- `mgit add .` in a repo with `.gitignore` (ignoring `ignored.txt` + `build/`) STAGED `build/out.o` and `ignored.txt` anyway. It DOES skip `.git/` and `.mgit/` (good), but nothing else.
- `mgit status` on mgit-dev lists a huge noisy untracked set — `.claude/worktrees/<...>/.git`, `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (inside leftover worktrees), build artifacts, the `mgit` binary, `cover.out`, etc. — because none of the .gitignore rules are applied.

IMPACT: this is the #1 blocker to adopting mgit on an existing repo (the bootstrap-cost friction in MGIT-26). A blanket working-tree import pulls in build output, vendored worktrees, and the compiled binary; status is unusable as a signal. It forces scoped per-file `mgit add`, defeating the "just works over your repo" coexistence story (MGIT-14).

FIX: make the working-tree walk used by `mgit add`/`mgit status` (and anything that enumerates untracked files) honor `.gitignore` (and ideally nested .gitignore + .git/info/exclude), consistent with the SEC-03 staging which already drops .mgit/.git at any depth. Likely lives near cmd/mgit/add.go + status.go + whatever walks the worktree (internal/store/git worktree materialize or a dedicated ignore matcher). Use a tested gitignore-matching approach (go-git has gitignore matchers: github.com/go-git/go-git/v5/plumbing/format/gitignore — already an approved dependency). Add tests: ignored file not staged by `add .`, ignored dir skipped, nested .gitignore honored, negation (`!`) honored, `.git`/`.mgit` always skipped.

TDD per CLAUDE.md; no co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer. This is the pilot task for the MGIT-26 dogfood (do it USING mgit's own micro-commit workflow, then squash/export the result to git for delivery). Refs: MGIT-26, MGIT-14.
nodes.acceptance: `mgit add .` and `mgit status` honor the repo's .gitignore (and nested .gitignore + .git/info/exclude), never staging/listing ignored paths, while still always skipping .git/ and .mgit/; covered by tests (ignored file/dir, nested, negation, .git/.mgit always skipped). On mgit-dev, `mgit status` after init shows a clean, signal-bearing untracked set (no build artifacts / worktrees / binary).
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: mgit→git delivery BROKEN: squash --to-git emits empty patch; mgit diff renders empty paths (2nd dogfood finding)
nodes.prompt:
CRITICAL DOGFOOD FINDING (2026-06-26, MGIT-26 pilot, during MGIT-32). The mgit→git delivery bridge — the whole point of the "checkpointed working substrate → squash → land to git" story ([[mgit-purpose-positioning]]) — does NOT work. Two micro-commits were made on task MGIT-32 (20310558 red test, c01561ac green fix), both committed cleanly via `mgit add`+`mgit commit`. Then:

1. `mgit squash --task-id MGIT-32 --to-git --to-git-output X.patch` produced an 11-line patch with the commit SUMMARY only and ZERO `diff --git` hunks — i.e. an EMPTY patch. The squashed changes are not rendered into the format-patch, so the work cannot be delivered to git via the documented bridge.
2. `mgit diff --task-id MGIT-32` renders garbage: repeated `diff --mgit a/ b/` blocks with EMPTY path names and "deleted file:" + `--- a/ (00000000) +++ b/ ()` — no real paths, no content, everything looks deleted-from-nothing.
3. `mgit show <commit>` prints commit metadata (author/date/task/type/message) but no file list / no diff.

The objects committed fine (mgit log shows the chain), so this is a DIFF/PATCH-RENDERING defect (the task/commit tree-diff against its base is not being computed/printed), not a storage loss. But it makes squash --to-git / diff / show useless and BLOCKS delivery of mgit-tracked work to git. I had to deliver MGIT-32 via plain `git add`+`git commit` instead (the working tree already held the changes because the edits were made directly on the shared tree, not in an isolated mgit worktree).

INVESTIGATE: the task/commit diff computation behind `mgit diff`, `mgit show`, and `mgit squash --to-git` (likely a shared diff renderer in internal/store/git or the diff/squash service). The empty `a/ b/` paths suggest the tree-walk that produces FileDiffs for a task is yielding entries with blank Path (or diffing a tree against itself/empty). Reproduce: fresh repo, mgit init, write a file, mgit add + commit --task-id T, then `mgit diff --task-id T` and `mgit squash --task-id T --to-git` — assert the diff/patch contain the file's real path + content. nodes.title: Wire mgit worktrees into the agent flow (close dogfood gap #5)
nodes.prompt:
DOGFOOD GAP #5 (MGIT-26): when an agent works a task, it currently runs in a GIT worktree (the Claude Code harness auto-isolates into git worktrees), NOT an mgit worktree — so the canonical "one task <-> one mgit worktree <-> one agent, commits auto-tagged" flow (FR-16) is never exercised by the agent. We CAN'T change the external harness, but we CAN make mgit's own agent-launch flow first-class: one command that starts an agent on a task inside an mgit-managed worktree, wired so the agent's commits are mgit-task-tagged and isolated, and `mgit run` routes its shell into the task sandbox.

VERIFIED WORKING (manually, 2026-06-26) so build on it: `mgit worktree add <path> --task <ID>` materializes the full tree from .mgit and binds the task; a `mgit commit` from inside that worktree auto-inherits the task id (FR-16); `mgit squash --task <ID> --to-git | git apply` round-trips. The pieces work — this task WIRES them into a cohesive agent entry flow.

SCOPE (design the cleanest cohesive flow; reuse existing pieces, do not reinvent):
- Reuse internal/worktree (the WorktreeManager / `mgit worktree add` path) to create+bind the mgit worktree for the task.
- Reuse internal/agentadapter (UpsertClaudeMd + WriteClaudeSettings, claude.go/claudemd.go) to write the worktree's CLAUDE.md (the working-discipline + sandbox-env block) and .claude/settings.json that routes the agent's shell through `mgit run` (the sandbox hook). See cmd/mgit/run.go (newRunCmd/resolveRun/sandboxForDir) for how `mgit run` binds a sandbox to a worktree dir.
- Deliver it as a first-class command — either extend `mgit worktree add` with agent-wiring flags (e.g. --agent claude that also writes the adapter files), or a new `mgit work`/`mgit agent start` command — whichever is cleaner and matches the existing CLI conventions. Optionally (behind a flag) launch the task sandbox bound to the worktree so `mgit run` works immediately; if the sandbox backend is unavailable, degrade gracefully (the worktree + adapter wiring must still succeed — fail-closed only the sandbox-routing part).
- Most of this is HOST-SIDE (worktree materialize + adapter file writes) and fully unit-testable WITHOUT a sandbox/KVM; only the optional sandbox-launch leg is env-gated.

TESTS: worktree created+bound to the task; CLAUDE.md + .claude/settings.json written into it with the mgit-run routing; a commit made in the worktree auto-tags the task; idempotent re-run; graceful degradation when the sandbox is unavailable. TDD per CLAUDE.md (red->green), godoc with Refs, no functions>50 lines / files>500.

CONSTRAINTS: no co-authored-by/agent/"Generated with" trailer in any commit; no LAN IP; full gate (gofmt/vet/golangci-lint 0/build/-race) before reporting. Do NOT mark mtix done and do NOT commit to main — work in your worktree and report the file paths + full contents + verification; the parent integrates + validates. Refs: MGIT-26, FR-16, MGIT-11.11.
nodes.acceptance: A first-class mgit command starts an agent on a task inside an mgit-managed worktree: it provisions+binds the mgit worktree (reusing WorktreeManager), writes the agentadapter CLAUDE.md + .claude/settings.json routing the agent's shell through `mgit run`, and (optionally/gated) launches the bound sandbox, degrading gracefully if unavailable. Commits made in that worktree auto-tag the task (FR-16). Covered by host-side tests (creation, adapter wiring, auto-tag, idempotency, graceful degradation); full gate green; no banned trailers; no LAN IP.

nodes.title: mgit/git tree drift when dogfooding over git: define the sync model + a one-command resync
nodes.prompt:
ADOPTION FRICTION (found 2026-06-26 dogfooding mgit on mgit-dev, MGIT-26). mgit runs OVER an existing git repo (MGIT-14 coexistence): the project's git tree and the .mgit store are TWO trees. When work is delivered via GIT directly (as MGIT-32/33/34 were — git commits 5138fd1/21756b9/40e6150), the .mgit store stays at its last import (bootstrap ac2ad8ff) and DRIFTS from git main. Concretely: `mgit work <path> --task <ID>` materializes the worktree from .mgit, so it produced a STALE tree (missing work.go etc.) until a manual re-import (`mgit add . && mgit commit`) re-synced .mgit to the current working tree. The drift was silent — nothing warned that the materialized worktree was behind git main.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the core coexistence question for adopting mgit on a repo that ALSO uses git for delivery. Two sources of truth that silently diverge = stale worktrees, confusing diffs, and lost confidence. It is the #1 friction for the "dogfood mgit on its own repo" story and any real user adopting mgit over an existing git repo.

ADDRESS CLEANLY (design-first — likely an ADR, NOT a band-aid). Decide + implement:
1. AUTHORITATIVE-SOURCE MODEL (the root decision; write it as an ADR): is mgit the working substrate with ALL changes flowing mgit -> squash -> land to git (so .mgit is always current and you NEVER commit to git directly while using mgit), OR is git authoritative and .mgit re-syncs from it on demand? Pick one and document the workflow + invariants. (This session mixed both, which is what caused the drift.)
2. ONE-COMMAND RESYNC: replace the ad-hoc `mgit add . && mgit commit` with a first-class, idempotent `mgit sync` (or extend `mgit import`) that brings .mgit's base up to the current git HEAD / working tree in one step (honoring .gitignore — fixed in MGIT-32). Fast, safe, documented.
3. DRIFT DETECTION + GUIDANCE: `mgit work` (and probably `mgit status`) should DETECT when .mgit's base tree diverges from the git working tree and warn (or offer to resync) BEFORE materializing a stale worktree — never silently materialize behind git.
4. Evaluate (and document the decision either way) whether `mgit work` should be able to materialize from the live working tree / git HEAD directly when bound to the base, vs always from .mgit — against the isolation model.

ACCEPTANCE: an ADR records the authoritative-source/sync model + workflow; a one-command resync exists (idempotent, gitignore-honoring, tested); drift between .mgit and the git working tree is detected and surfaced (not silent) by `mgit work`/`status`; docs (README + the agent skill from MGIT-29) describe the chosen workflow so adopters don't hit silent drift. TDD per CLAUDE.md; no co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer; no LAN IP. Refs: MGIT-26, MGIT-14, MGIT-32, MGIT-34.
nodes.acceptance: An ADR records the authoritative-source + sync model (mgit-as-substrate-with-land vs git-authoritative-with-resync) and the resulting workflow/invariants. A first-class idempotent resync (`mgit sync` or extended `mgit import`) brings .mgit current with git HEAD/working tree, honoring .gitignore, with tests. `mgit work` and `mgit status` detect + surface .mgit↔git drift instead of silently materializing a stale worktree. README + the MGIT-29 agent skill document the chosen workflow. Gate green; no banned trailers; no LAN IP.

nodes.title: Cut a release — main is 208 commits ahead of v0.1.0-beta; the entire usable product is UNRELEASED
nodes.prompt:
CRITICAL ADOPTION BLOCKER, found by a hands-on trial on a DIFFERENT project (2026-06-26): the owner installed mgit elsewhere and it could not deliver value — `mgit worktree add` reported success but materialized NO directory, and `work`/`sandbox`/`run` were absent from the binary. ROOT CAUSE: the latest release is v0.1.0-beta and `main` (HEAD e102afe) is **208 commits ahead** of it. The installed binary (brew/go-install resolve to the release) predates ESSENTIALLY THE WHOLE PRODUCT: worktree materialization (MGIT-17), the FR-17 microVM sandbox + `mgit run`/`sandbox`, `mgit work` (MGIT-34), the coexistence/dogfood fixes (MGIT-14/32/33). VERIFIED: on current main, `mgit worktree add <abs> --task MGIT-2.1` DOES materialize (6 files) and `work`/`sandbox`/`run` all exist — so the value is real, just unshipped.

IMPACT: this is plausibly the #1 adoption blocker — "if we don't ship it, no one can use it." Every external trial will hit a 208-commit-old broken binary. It dwarfs any individual bug.

DECISION + ACTIONS:
1. Decide the release cut: a fresh BETA now (e.g. v0.2.0-beta) to unblock trials immediately, vs waiting for the remaining v1 items (MGIT-35 coexistence, MGIT-31 firecracker live numbers, the remaining 11.x hardening). Recommendation: cut a beta NOW — the sandbox/work/run/materialization value is real, validated (vzf live + the canonical loop), and CI-green; gating a release on every v1 item keeps users on a binary that genuinely doesn't work.
2. Run the release: the Release workflow exists (.github/workflows/release.yml) + homebrew-tap dispatch (commit 015a043). Version-bump, tag, build cross-platform binaries, publish, and verify `brew`/`go install` deliver the new binary with `work`/`sandbox`/`run` + working worktree materialization.
3. Smoke-test the released artifact on a clean machine/repo: `mgit init` -> `mgit work --task <ID>` materializes -> commit -> squash --to-git applies. Don't declare released-good without installing the published binary and running the loop.
4. Note known current rough edges to mention in release notes (or fix first): the `worktree add --task` vs `commit --task-id` flag inconsistency (MGIT-37).

No co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer; no LAN IP in release notes.
nodes.acceptance: A new release is cut and published such that `brew install`/`go install` deliver a binary containing worktree materialization + `mgit work`/`sandbox`/`run`; the released artifact is smoke-tested on a clean repo (init -> work materializes -> commit -> squash --to-git applies); release notes list the headline capabilities + known rough edges. A documented decision on beta-now vs wait-for-v1.

nodes.title: Worktree seed excludes build-required gitignored artifacts (e.g. embedded web/dist) — full build needs them
nodes.prompt:
FRICTION (minor) found 2026-06-26 by another team's full real run of mgit. The gitignore-aware worktree seed (MGIT-32) correctly excludes git-ignored junk (no node_modules — praised) BUT also excludes git-ignored BUILD-REQUIRED artifacts: e.g. a generated `web/dist` that the Go binary `//go:embed`s. Result: a fresh mgit worktree can run PACKAGE-SCOPED tests fine, but `go build ./...` fails because the embedded dist isn't present. (Note: a plain git worktree has the SAME gap — gitignored generated artifacts aren't in a fresh checkout either; you'd run the generate/build step. So this is partly git-normal, not unique to mgit.)

OPTIONS (decide + document):
1. DOCUMENT as expected: gitignored generated artifacts are not seeded; the worktree must run the generate/build step (e.g. `npm run build` to produce web/dist) before a full `go build ./...`, exactly as with a fresh git checkout. Add this to the README + MGIT_WORKING_DISCIPLINE.md and to `mgit work`'s output/next-steps hint when it detects likely-embedded generated dirs.
2. OPT-IN include for build-required ignored paths: a `--include-ignored <glob>` flag on `mgit work` (and/or a `.mgit/seed-include` config) that force-carries specific gitignored-but-build-required paths (web/dist) into the seed while STILL excluding everything else (node_modules etc.). This bridges the gap for embed-heavy repos without reimporting junk. Materialize from the source working tree when the path exists there.
Recommendation: ship (1) now (cheap, honest, git-correct) and add (2) as the convenience for embed-heavy projects. TDD per CLAUDE.md; no co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer. Refs: MGIT-32, MGIT-34, MGIT-28.
nodes.acceptance: Documented behavior: a worktree's gitignored generated artifacts (e.g. web/dist) are not seeded and must be regenerated for a full build — surfaced in README + the agent skill + ideally a `mgit work` hint. Optionally: a `--include-ignored <glob>` (or `.mgit/seed-include`) opt-in that carries specified build-required ignored paths into the seed while still excluding node_modules etc., with tests. No banned trailers.

nodes.title: MGIT-35 follow-ups: gitref LFS detection, fingerprint cost at scale, --base ref polish
nodes.description: Deferred-but-tracked hardening items from the MGIT-35 (ADR-008 auto-housekeeping) implementation + its independent review (main 52adfe4). None are acceptance gaps for MGIT-35; they are the clearly-flagged follow-ups. Refs: MGIT-35, ADR-008.
nodes.prompt:
Hardening follow-ups deferred from MGIT-35 (ADR-008 auto-housekeeping; shipped on main 52adfe4). Address when each becomes load-bearing:

1. git-LFS pointers (internal/store/gitref): the read-only .git reader does NOT detect LFS-tracked files; an LFS pointer would be captured as its small text pointer rather than real content when the base is synced from a working tree with un-smudged LFS files. Detect (e.g. .gitattributes filter=lfs, or the pointer signature) and either fail loud (ErrUnsupportedGitState) or degrade clearly. Add a gitref test.

2. Working-tree fingerprint cost at scale (internal/store/git/sync.go WorkingTreeFingerprint): the drift gate sha256-hashes every trackable working file on every base-dependent command (status/diff/work). Fine for normal repos; the ADR-008 safety review flagged it as not cheap for large monorepos. Add a benchmark; if needed, add a cheaper first-pass signal (e.g. compare git HEAD commit-id first and only fingerprint on HEAD-equal-but-maybe-dirty, or a size/mtime pre-filter that still falls back to content hash) without reintroducing the mtime false-negative.

3. `mgit work --base <ref>` ref resolution (internal/service/worktree.go resolveBaseCommit): currently resolves an mgit commit hash, an mgit branch name, or HEAD. It does NOT resolve a ref that exists only in the project's git (e.g. a git tag), which would need a read-only git object read via gitref. Add if hotfix-from-git-tag becomes a real need.

4. Minor UX: re-running `mgit work --base X` on an ALREADY-EXISTING task branch silently ignores --base (resolveForkBase returns the existing tip before the --base branch). Decide: error on conflicting explicit --base, or document the resume semantics. Also `mgit worktree add` has no --base flag (only `mgit work` does) — add for parity if worktree add is used directly for pinned bases.

TDD per CLAUDE.md; no banned trailers; no LAN IP.
nodes.acceptance: gitref detects git-LFS and fails-loud-or-degrades (tested); a benchmark exists for the drift-gate fingerprint and the common path is demonstrably cheap (or an optimization landed); --base ref-resolution behavior for project-.git-only refs is implemented or explicitly documented as out of scope; the re-run --base no-op and worktree-add --base parity are resolved or documented. Gate green.

nodes.title: branch --delete leaves a stale row in the SQLite branch index → worktree add for the same task-id fails "branch already exists"
nodes.description: External bug report (2026-06-29, the team building their feature on mgit v0.2.0-beta, darwin/arm64). Medium severity: after `mgit branch --delete`, the task can NEVER receive a new worktree (no clean recovery via gc/prune); only workaround is a different task-id. Root cause CONFIRMED in code. Refs: MGIT-26.
nodes.prompt:
A task branch deleted via `mgit branch --delete` disappears from `mgit branch` (the ref/list view) but `mgit worktree add --task <same-id>` then fails with `create branch in index: branch already exists`. gc and worktree prune do not fix it; re-deleting idempotently "succeeds" but the error persists. The only workaround is using a different task-id.

REPRO (from the reporter):
  mgit branch                                   # task/MTIX-30.8 exists
  mgit branch --delete task/MTIX-30.8 --force   # "Deleted branch task/MTIX-30.8"
  mgit branch | grep -c MTIX-30.8               # 0 — gone from the list
  mgit worktree add /tmp/wt --task MTIX-30.8    # Error: create branch: create branch in index: branch already exists: task/MTIX-30.8

ROOT CAUSE (confirmed in code): branch state lives in TWO stores and delete only touches one.
- `internal/store/index/branches.go` has CreateBranch/GetBranch/UpdateBranchHead/Lock/Unlock/ListBranches but NO DeleteBranch — the SQLite `branches` table (PK = name) has no delete path.
- `internal/service/branch.go` `DeleteBranch` is `return s.gitBranches.DeleteBranch(ctx, name, force)` — it removes the go-git REF only, never the index row.
- `BranchService.CreateBranch` (the path `worktree add` uses) calls `s.indexStore.CreateBranch` which INSERTs into `branches`; the lingering row makes it fail "branch already exists".
- `mgit branch` (list) reads the ref store (branch gone) while `worktree add`'s create-branch check reads the index (row remains) → the two views disagree. gc only packs objects, prune only checks worktree registry rows — neither clears the branch index row.

FIX DIRECTION: make branch deletion consistent across both stores in one operation.
1. Add `index.Store.DeleteBranch(ctx, name)` (parameterized DELETE in a WriteTx; tolerate row-absent so it's idempotent/recovery-friendly).
2. `BranchService.DeleteBranch` deletes from the ref store AND the index — and should clear the index row even when the ref is already gone (so existing stuck tasks recover). Consider deleting the index row first/independently so a half-state self-heals.
3. (Optional, defensive) `worktree add`'s create-branch path could treat an index row with no matching ref as reusable rather than a hard conflict.
NOTE: `branches` is NOT the append-only audit table (`task_commits` is); deleting a `branches` row is fine and does not violate FR-12.

REQUIRED TESTS:
- TestBranchService_DeleteBranch_RemovesFromIndexAndRef (delete clears the index row)
- TestWorktreeAdd_AfterBranchDelete_Succeeds (init → worktree add T → worktree remove T → branch --delete T → worktree add T succeeds — the reporter's exact regression)
- TestBranchService_DeleteBranch_RefMissingIndexPresent_StillClears (recovery for already-stuck tasks)

SECONDARY FINDINGS (same area — minor; split out if preferred, but don't lose them):
(a) UX: `mgit branch -D task/X` → "unknown shorthand flag: 'D'", and delete takes the name as a flag value not a positional. git users expect `mgit branch -d/-D <name>` (positional). Add -d/-D aliases + accept a positional branch name for delete.
(b) No cleanup path for stale task-branches: with the git-canonical integration pattern (`mgit squash --task-id <id> --to-git | git apply`), task/ branches are never reaped and accumulate (8+ lingering after a sprint). Combined with this bug they also can't be cleanly removed. Add `mgit branch --prune-merged` (or auto-reap after `squash --to-git`/land) for teams keeping git canonical.

CLAUDE.md: TDD red→green; no co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer; no LAN IP. Refs: MGIT-26, MGIT-22 (squash semantics), FR-16 (worktrees), FR-5 (branches).
nodes.acceptance: `mgit branch --delete <name>` removes the branch from BOTH the go-git ref store and the SQLite branch index in one operation, and clears a stale index row even when the ref is already absent (so currently-stuck tasks recover). After delete, `mgit worktree add --task <same-id>` re-creates the branch+worktree cleanly. Regression test covers init→worktree add→remove→branch delete→worktree add success. Secondary: -d/-D aliases + positional name accepted; a prune path for merged/squashed-out task branches exists or is split into its own tracked ticket. Gate green; no banned trailers; no LAN IP.

nodes.title: Branch-lifecycle UX/robustness follow-ups (from MGIT-42)
nodes.description: Minor, non-blocking items surfaced during the MGIT-42 RCA/fix (main 04827fd) + the original external report. None block the team (MGIT-42's core fix landed). Tracked so they aren't lost. Refs: MGIT-42, MGIT-26.
nodes.prompt:
Branch-lifecycle polish, found during MGIT-42 (branch --delete index-consistency fix). All minor / UX / robustness:

1. index.Store.CreateBranch conflates errors. `internal/store/index/branches.go` maps ANY INSERT error to model.ErrBranchAlreadyExists — so a transient DB error is misreported as "branch already exists" (and would mislead the self-heal path added in MGIT-42, which only truly applies to a uniqueness conflict). Distinguish a UNIQUE/PK violation from other errors (inspect the modernc/sqlite error, or pre-check), returning ErrBranchAlreadyExists only for the real conflict.

2. CLI `mgit branch --delete` prints "Deleted branch <name>" even when the ref was already absent (the service now tolerates ErrBranchNotFound for recovery — good — but the message is then misleading). Consider reporting what actually happened (e.g. "cleared stale index entry" vs "deleted branch"), or at least not implying a ref was removed when none existed.

3. git-style delete UX: `mgit branch -D <name>` / `-d <name>` are unsupported (only `--delete <name> --force`). git users expect `-d`/`-D` and a positional branch name. Add the aliases + accept a positional name for delete.

4. No cleanup path for stale task branches. With the git-canonical integration pattern (`mgit squash --task-id <id> --to-git | git apply`), task/<id> branches are never reaped and accumulate (the reporting team had 8+ lingering). Add `mgit branch --prune-merged` (or auto-reap after a successful squash --to-git / land) so teams keeping git canonical can clean up.

TDD per CLAUDE.md; no co-authored-by/agent/Generated-with trailer; no LAN IP. Refs: MGIT-42, MGIT-26, FR-5.
nodes.acceptance: index CreateBranch returns ErrBranchAlreadyExists only on a real uniqueness conflict (other errors surfaced distinctly), with a test; `branch --delete` messaging is accurate when the ref was already absent; `-d`/`-D` aliases + positional name accepted with a CLI test; a prune path for merged/squashed-out task branches exists (or is explicitly deferred with rationale). nodes.title: MCP worktree tools are stubs returning "not yet available (Wave 11)" while README claims them
nodes.description: internal/mcp/server.go:304-312: mgit_worktree_add/list/remove return the literal text "worktree add/list/remove: not yet available (Wave 11)" with a success result. This violates the anti-stub law (CLAUDE.md Development Rule 11: stub code that compiles but does nothing is active deception) and the README/MCP docs advertise 15 tools including all three worktree tools. External trial 2026-07-03: the agent burned a session discovering this ("the MCP tool for worktrees isn't wired up yet, even if the CLI supports it").
nodes.prompt: Either implement the three MCP worktree tools by delegating to the same service layer the CLI uses (WorktreeService Add/List/Remove; note the server already holds the repo lock so no lock conflict), or unregister them and correct every doc that claims them (README MCP section, mgit docs generate templates). Implementing is strongly preferred: worktree add via MCP is exactly what a driving agent needs, and it sidesteps the serve-lock starvation (see companion lock ticket). Stubs returning fake success text must not survive either way. TDD: table-driven tests per tool, error paths included.

nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: Long-running `mgit serve` holds the exclusive repo lock for its lifetime, starving all CLI use
nodes.description: External trial 2026-07-03: with `mgit serve --mcp-only` running (an agent's MCP server, up ~1 day), every CLI command failed "another mgit process is running: held by PID ...". RCA confirmed: every command path goes through newApp which acquires .mgit/locks/mgit.lock (cmd/mgit/app.go:70, internal/store/lock/lock.go) and `mgit serve` blocks holding it until shutdown. So CLI and a long-running MCP/REST server are mutually exclusive by construction, which defeats the standard usage pattern: an agent driving mgit over MCP while a human (or a second agent) uses the CLI on the same repo. The 30s Acquire timeout turns every CLI call into a 30-second hang followed by an error.
nodes.prompt: Design and implement finer-grained locking so a long-running server and the CLI can coexist. Recommended direction: the server stops holding the process lock for its lifetime and instead acquires it per-operation (same scope a CLI command holds it), relying on SQLite WAL + busy_timeout and go-git store atomicity underneath; read-only commands (log/status/show/diff/audit/verify) could further take a shared lock or none. This is a concurrency-critical change: enumerate every writer seam (index writes, go-git refs/objects, HEAD, worktree registry), define the lock scope for each, and cover with -race concurrency tests (CLI hammering during server operation). Alternative worth evaluating and documenting if chosen instead: CLI transparently proxies to the running server when the lock is held. Keep the error message actionable either way (name the holder command, not just the PID).
nodes.acceptance: `mgit serve --mcp-only` running + `mgit status`/`commit`/`worktree add` from the CLI both succeed concurrently, verified by a test. No 30s hang. -race clean. Documented concurrency model.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: Sandbox-less `mgit work` wiring breaks and misleads the agent (shims route to fail-closed run; CLAUDE.md overstates)
nodes.description: On a machine without mgit-sandboxd, `mgit work` (no --sandbox, or sandbox leg degraded) still installs the full routing wiring: PATH shims that exec every invoked command through `mgit run` (internal/agentadapter/shims.go), which is hard fail-closed ("no fallback", cmd/mgit/sandbox_connect.go:100), and a CLAUDE.md block stating "Your shell already routes through `mgit run`, so just run commands normally" (internal/agentadapter/claudemd.go:73). External trial 2026-07-03: the agent followed the wiring, hit the fail-closed error on everything (couldn't "even echo"), and concluded mgit is unusable as a working substrate. Note the Claude PreToolUse hook DOES degrade correctly (returns "ask" when no sandbox is routable, claude_hook.go); the defects are the unconditional shims and the unconditional CLAUDE.md wording.
nodes.prompt: Make the worktree wiring sandbox-aware: (1) when no sandbox is bound/routable, the CLAUDE.md env block must say so explicitly ("no sandbox on this machine: run commands normally; containment is unavailable until mgit-sandboxd is installed", with the install pointer) instead of claiming routing is active; (2) decide shim behavior without a daemon: either do not install shims until a sandbox is launched, or make the shim fall back to direct exec WITH a visible warning ONLY when the worktree was never sandbox-bound (never silently bypass a requested sandbox; NFR-17.6 fail-closed must hold whenever containment was requested); (3) `mgit work` output should state the containment status in one line the agent can parse. Keep the security invariant crisp: fail-closed when a sandbox was requested or previously active; honest-open when containment was never available. Update agent docs/skills accordingly.
nodes.acceptance: On a daemon-less machine: `mgit work` produces a worktree where an agent can build/test normally, CLAUDE.md tells the truth about containment status, and no shim hard-fails basic commands. On a sandboxed worktree: routing still fail-closed. Tests cover both postures.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: Install-channel + sandbox e2e coverage in CI (clean-machine, all channels, both postures)
nodes.description: Both external trials (2026-06-26 and 2026-07-03) failed on distribution, not product: gaps that existed only on a CLEAN machine installing via a real channel, which no CI job exercises. CI today runs unit/integration/e2e from the repo checkout, where dev-built binaries (mgit-sandboxd next to mgit) mask exactly the failures users hit. Nothing validates: brew install, go install, release-archive extraction, running with NO mgit-sandboxd present, or the full sandbox path from published artifacts.
nodes.prompt: Add CI e2e coverage for what a real user gets. (1) Install-channel matrix job (post-release and nightly-on-main-snapshot): install via release archive + go install (and brew where a runner allows), then on a scratch repo run the core loop (init, work, commit, log, squash --to-git | git apply round-trip, worktree add/list/remove, verify, audit) asserting real behavior, not just exit codes. (2) Daemon-less posture job: with mgit-sandboxd absent, assert `mgit work` yields a usable worktree, wiring is honest (per MGIT-47 behavior), `mgit run` fails with the actionable install pointer, and basic agent commands still work. (3) Sandbox posture job: with mgit-sandboxd from the same artifact set, run `mgit run -- echo ok` + a land round-trip; Linux needs a KVM-capable runner (self-hosted KVM box or nested-virt), macOS arm64 runner for vzf; gate gracefully where hosts lack virtualization, but the RELEASE checklist must include at least one live pass per platform. (4) MCP posture job: start `mgit serve --mcp-only`, drive every documented MCP tool via a scripted client. Wire these into release.yml as gates. Respect: KVM-box LAN IP never appears in the repo/CI logs (refer to it as the Linux runner).
nodes.acceptance: CI has jobs for install-channel matrix, daemon-less posture, sandbox posture (or documented env-gate + release-checklist live pass), and MCP-driven loop. A regression like "sandboxd missing from archives" or "MCP tool returns placeholder" fails CI before users see it.

MGIT-49 removed the false README claim rather than pretend. Current protection is localhost binding (127.0.0.1 default) only. nodes.prompt: Decide and implement: either (a) wire token auth end-to-end: `mgit token generate/rotate/revoke/list` CLI, SHA-256-hashed storage, Bearer middleware on every REST route, covered by tests including auth-failure paths, and re-document; or (b) delete the dead TokenStore code and document the security model as localhost-only + same-UID trust (matching the daemon socket's peer-credential posture). Do not leave dead security code in the tree: it reads as a control that does not exist. If (a), treat tokens as secrets (never logged); if (b), the bind-address config must refuse non-localhost without an explicit acknowledged flag.
nodes.acceptance: Either every REST route enforces Bearer auth with tests, or TokenStore is gone and the documented security model matches the code. No dead auth code. README/docs match the shipped behavior.

nodes.title: Close the flagship-claims vs e2e-proof gap: course-correction, REST posture, two-process lock coexistence, full MCP drive, feature→e2e matrix
nodes.description: Audit 2026-07-04: CI e2e (MGIT-48) covers the primary agent loop and the trial-failure regressions, but several flagship claims have no e2e proof: the course-correction loop (rollback → checkout -b → cherry-pick → squash) — the README's second pillar — is not e2e'd anywhere; REST has no e2e job; serve/CLI lock coexistence (MGIT-46's headline) is tested in-process only, never as two real processes; 11 of 15 MCP tools are only registration-checked through the real stdio server; and there is no living map of feature→e2e coverage, so gaps stay invisible. Also core_loop.sh's header claims it tests `status` but never calls it.
nodes.prompt: Extend the e2e suite (scripts/e2e/, wired into e2e.yml + make e2e): (1) course_correction.sh — drive the full backtrack/fork/salvage loop against an installed binary: micro-commits with a bad step, rollback (assert append-only revert, no history deletion), checkout the good point, checkout -b a new line, cherry-pick the still-good work, squash, and assert the abandoned line remains in history/audit; verify every command/flag against the CLI first, not the README. (2) rest_posture.sh — start `mgit serve --api-only` as a real process, drive the documented /api/v1 routes (health, commits create/get/list, task commits, branches, squash, rollback, verify) with curl, assert real JSON behavior and the 127.0.0.1-only bind. (3) In the same script or a sibling: two-process lock coexistence — while serve runs, CLI commit/status/worktree commands in the same repo must succeed promptly (no 'another mgit process', no 30s stall). (4) Extend mcpdrive to CALL every registered tool through the real stdio server (commit/status/log/show/branch/diff/export/audit/config/squash/rollback), not just list them. (5) docs/E2E-MATRIX.md — feature × e2e-job matrix marking e2e-proven / unit-only / env-gated / uncovered (Windows stays visible as uncovered), linked from MCP-PARITY.md; update it whenever jobs change. (6) Fix core_loop.sh's status overclaim by adding a real `mgit status` assertion.

REST routes and serve+CLI coexistence proven with real processes. Every registered MCP tool is invoked through stdio. E2E-MATRIX.md exists and matches the jobs. core_loop.sh tests what its header claims.

nodes.title: rollback and cherry-pick are record-level only: FileDiffs never reach the commit tree (no content restoration)
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-04 while e2e-proving the course-correction loop (MGIT-53), verified in code AND empirically. Shared root cause: the store builds every commit tree from HEAD + CLI staging only (internal/store/git/commit.go buildTreeFromStaging, line ~72) and does not persist FileDiffs into git objects (comment at line ~353). Consequences: (1) RollbackTask (internal/service/rollback.go) computes inverseDiffs and sets them on the revert commit, but the resulting tree is BYTE-IDENTICAL to pre-revert (empirically confirmed): rollback records intent in the append-only history/audit but restores no content. (2) cherry-pick's picked diffs are provenance metadata only: deleting a file then cherry-picking its "add" commit produced a tree still lacking the file (empirically confirmed). Also: rollback is task-scoped only (the positional/--commit hash merely resolves the owning task; there is no single-commit revert). Byte-level salvage today is per-file `mgit restore <file> --commit <hash>`. The README was corrected (2026-07-04) to describe the real semantics; the e2e (scripts/e2e/course_correction.sh) asserts current behavior and must be updated alongside any fix. Relevant prior art: MGIT-16 built a BuildTree mode which may be the mechanism for applying diffs to trees.
nodes.prompt: Make rollback and cherry-pick content-restoring, or explicitly decide record-level is the design and make the CLI say so. Strong recommendation: content-restoring — an agent that cannot mechanically recover a known-good state loses the substrate's core promise ("recover to a known-good checkpoint"). Design sketch: give the commit path a mode that materializes a commit from an explicit tree transformation (apply FileDiffs / inverse diffs onto the parent tree — evaluate reusing MGIT-16's BuildTree mode) instead of HEAD+staging; rollback then produces a revert commit whose tree actually reverses the task's changes (and updates the worktree), and cherry-pick applies the picked commit's changes to the target branch's tree (with a conflict story: fail with a clear error on overlap, no silent merge). Also decide single-commit rollback (--commit currently resolves the whole task): either implement per-commit revert or make the flag's semantics explicit in help/docs. TDD at service+store level (table-driven: revert restores bytes; cherry-pick materializes; conflicts error; append-only preserved; idempotence), update course_correction.sh to assert the new semantics, and update README/agent docs/E2E-MATRIX accordingly.
nodes.acceptance: After rollback, the working tree and new commit tree no longer contain the reverted changes (byte-asserted). After cherry-pick, the picked commit's content exists on the target (byte-asserted). Conflicts fail loudly. Append-only preserved. course_correction.sh asserts content, not just records. Docs match.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: checkout cannot target a commit hash: no way to move the worktree to an arbitrary checkpoint
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-04 during MGIT-53. `mgit checkout` accepts branch names only (cmd/mgit/checkout.go, cobra.ExactArgs(1) → CheckoutService.Checkout, no hash resolution), and `checkout -b` creates at current HEAD only. The README used to instruct `mgit checkout <good-hash>` (corrected 2026-07-04); today the only checkpoint-recovery primitive is per-file `mgit restore <file> --commit <hash>`. For an agent, "go back to checkpoint X wholesale" is a natural, mechanical operation the substrate should offer.
nodes.prompt: Add a whole-tree checkpoint recovery primitive. Options to evaluate: (a) `mgit checkout <hash>` materializing that commit's tree into the worktree with a detached/pinned state recorded (plus `checkout -b <name>` from there to fork), or (b) a simpler `mgit restore --all --commit <hash>` (restore every file from the checkpoint) that avoids detached-HEAD semantics entirely. Recommendation: (b) first — it composes with the existing verified loop (restore-all → commit → continue) and needs no new HEAD states; (a) can follow if agents need true detached inspection. Guard rails: refuse with a clear error when uncommitted changes would be overwritten (consistent with checkout's current block-on-dirty behavior). TDD; extend course_correction.sh to use the new primitive for the salvage step; update README/agent docs/E2E-MATRIX. Depends on/relates to MGIT-54 (shared goal: mechanical recovery to known-good state).
nodes.acceptance: An agent can recover the full working tree to any prior checkpoint with one command, byte-asserted in tests and in course_correction.sh. Dirty-tree overwrites are refused with a clear error. Docs match.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: ADR-008 auto-sync during `status` absorbs pre-first-commit changes, emptying the task's net diff
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-04 during MGIT-53's MCP e2e work, reproduced identically via CLI: `mgit add` → `mgit status` → `mgit commit --task-id T` → `mgit diff --task-id T` yields an EMPTY task diff. Cause: `status` runs the ADR-008 EnsureSynced housekeeping, which absorbs new working files into a `[mgit-sync]` base commit; the task's first commit then has no delta against the already-absorbed base. The commit itself is fine (content is in history), but the task's NET DIFF — the review surface, the squash content, the blast-radius answer — is silently empty. An agent that checks status mid-flow (agents do this constantly) silently loses its task attribution for those files. The MCP e2e (scripts/e2e/mcpdrive) had to be ordered around this; the workaround note is in its comments.
nodes.prompt: Decide and fix the staging-vs-resync interaction. Direction to evaluate first: EnsureSynced must treat mgit-STAGED paths (and plausibly all uncommitted worktree changes in a task-bound worktree) as task work-in-progress and exclude them from the [mgit-sync] base absorption — the base should advance on the project's git state, not on the task's pending work. Check ADR-008's staging-neutral resync guarantee (MGIT-35 H2 made resync staging-neutral for the SNAPSHOT; this finding is about base-content absorption, a different seam). Add regression tests: add → status → commit → task diff must show the change, in both a repo root and a bound worktree, via CLI and MCP; then remove the ordering workaround from scripts/e2e/mcpdrive and assert the natural order works.
nodes.acceptance: add → status → commit → `mgit diff --task-id` shows the change (CLI + MCP, root + worktree). mcpdrive drives the natural order without workarounds. ADR-008 doc updated if the absorption rule changes.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: `mgit run` inside a worktree spawns a doomed second daemon and never matches the sandbox (work --sandbox flow broken)
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-04 running the mandatory macOS live sandbox pass against the published v0.3.0-beta artifacts. The README's headline flow (`mgit work ./wt --task-id X --sandbox` then `cd wt; mgit run -- ...`) fails end-to-end for TWO independent reasons, both real code paths (not test artifacts): (1) productionSandboxConnect (cmd/mgit/sandbox_connect.go) keyed the daemon socket + host-root + --repo-root on the raw cwd; from inside a linked worktree (whose .mgit is a marker+shims dir, not the store) it spawned a SECOND daemon pointed at the worktree as host-root, which died ("open sandbox audit index: ... out of memory (14)"). (2) `mgit work wt` recorded the sandbox's WorktreePath verbatim (relative "wt"), while `mgit run` matched against an absolute, symlink-resolved cwd (/var vs /private/var on macOS), so sandboxForDir never matched → "no sandbox bound". Either alone breaks the documented flow.
nodes.prompt: FIXED in the same session (commit pending): (1) added sandboxRepoRoot(cwd) — resolve the OWNING repo via findRepoRoot + ReadWorktreeMarker, so a worktree routes to the shared PARENT's daemon/socket/host-root; productionSandboxConnect and the --repo-root spawn arg now use it. (2) added canonicalPath(p) (abs + EvalSymlinks, best-effort) and applied it at the record sides (mgit work, sandbox launch WorktreePath) AND the match side (resolveRun cwd), so both reduce to one spelling. Regression tests: TestSandboxRepoRoot_* (worktree/subdir/parent resolution) and TestRun_SymlinkedCwdAndRelativeRecord_StillMatches. Verify the full gate is green and the sandbox_posture.sh live pass gets past launch+routing (it does — it now reaches the guest vsock handshake). This ticket = the routing/path bugs only; the vsock-handshake issue on the locally-rebuilt macOS kernel is separate (see MGIT-30 reproducibility).
nodes.acceptance: `mgit work wt --task-id X --sandbox --image REF` then `cd wt && mgit run -- echo ok` resolves the parent repo's daemon and matches the bound sandbox (no second daemon, no "no sandbox bound"). Regression tests cover worktree daemon-root resolution and symlinked/relative path matching. Full gate green.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: `mgit run` races guest boot: daemon lazy-boot first-exec dials vsock before the guest listener is up (handshake EOF)
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-06 on the first LIVE KVM sandbox pass (the Linux runner, firecracker v1.16.0, current main 165714e + MGIT-57 fix, cached image vmlinux-5.10.223 + mgit-guest.ext4). `mgit run` — the headline sandbox verb — fails DETERMINISTICALLY with `sandbox exec: kvm exec: dial guest: fcvsock: read handshake reply: EOF` (3/3 retries, not a transient race between calls). Daemon-log timing is decisive: `sandbox launched` (backend=kvm) at T=22.038, `exec failed` EOF at T=22.436 — the first exec dials the guest vsock ~0.4s after a LAZY launch (created-state, FR-17.10 boot-on-first-exec), but the guest needs ~1.15s to boot and bind vsock 1024, so the dial hits a not-yet-listening endpoint and the connection resets. CRUCIAL SCOPE: the sandbox itself is PROVEN GOOD live — the in-process firecracker e2e harness passes on this exact box+image for real-guest land round-trip, notify auto-land, guest-root overlay drive, all 3 SEC-03 HostileGuest tests, and egress-none (which execs in-guest). The gap is ONLY the daemon-mediated lazy-boot→first-exec path (mgit CLI → mgit-sandboxd → backend), which NO harness test exercises with a real guest — so it shipped invisibly.
nodes.prompt: Make the daemon's lazy-boot exec wait for guest vsock readiness before (or while) dialing. Options: (a) bounded retry/backoff on the fcvsock dial+handshake in the kvm/vzf exec path (retry the connect until the guest answers or a deadline ~5-10s), and/or (b) gate the created→running boot so the first exec blocks until the guest's control vsock (1024) accepts a handshake, mirroring whatever readiness the in-process harness relies on. Prefer a shared readiness wait in the backend dial so BOTH backends (firecracker + vzf) benefit — the macOS vzf live pass shows the same guest-handshake symptom, likely the same race. Add a LIVE-gated regression: extend scripts/e2e/sandbox_posture.sh (already run on the box) to be the reproducer; also add a daemon-level test that lazy-launches then immediately execs against a fake/slow-booting guest and asserts the dial waits rather than EOFs. Re-validate on the KVM box (the Linux runner) until `sandbox_posture.sh` prints PASS (live). This BLOCKS the v0.3.1-beta sandbox-usability claim: mgit run must work end-to-end via the CLI, not just in-process.
nodes.acceptance: `mgit work wt --sandbox --image REF` then `cd wt && mgit run -- echo ok` prints ok on the KVM box (and macOS) — no handshake EOF. sandbox_posture.sh prints "SANDBOX POSTURE E2E: PASS (live)" on the Linux runner. A daemon/backend regression test covers lazy-boot-then-immediate-exec readiness. Fix applies to both firecracker and vzf dial paths.
nodes.creator: mcp

nodes.title: 3 firecracker e2e tests use a stale hardcoded image digest and fail (fixture bug, not a product defect)
nodes.description: Found 2026-07-06 during the live KVM run. TestE2E_ClaimToLand_Succeeds, TestE2E_ProvenanceRecordedPerCommit, and TestE2E_RemoveDiscardsUnlanded_NoResidue (internal/sandboxd/backend/firecracker/e2e_workflow_linux_test.go) fail fast (~0.2s, before any VM boot) with: `resolve image "mgit-guest@sha256:e2e0000...0001": verification failed: ref digest sha256:e2e0...0001 != lock digest sha256:<real>`. nodes.title: EPIC: Sandbox-active milestone — brew install → mgit run --sandbox works with no manual image build
nodes.description:
Today (v0.3.1-beta) ships the entitled/codesigned mgit-sandboxd, but the guest image (kernel + rootfs) must still be hand-built by each user — during live validation this session I had to rebuild the arm64 vz kernel (kernel.org rotated 6.6 LTS off mirrors → 6.12.74) and assemble a busybox-musl rootfs by hand. So the sandbox is INSTALLED but not ACTIVE out of the box. This epic makes it active: a brew/go-install user can run `mgit run --sandbox` against a shipped, digest-pinned, signed guest image with zero manual build.

TRUST MODEL DECISION (2026-07-21): v1 uses LOCAL-TRUST, the existing mechanism — the image is digest-pinned (sha256 in the fetch + images.lock) and Ed25519-signed at registration into the user's own trust root (images.GenerateTrustRoot/Register); brew's sha256 pin + GitHub HTTPS is the distribution integrity, the existing fail-closed boot verification is the runtime guarantee. This satisfies "digest-pinned signed guest image" with NO irreversible baked key. Distribution-trust (a HyperSwe release pubkey baked into mgit, images signed by a release-held private key) is a deliberate later upgrade, tracked separately — it is hard to reverse (ships in every binary) so it is not v1.

Components: (1) reproducible/pinned image+kernel build for both backends [MGIT-30 macOS + Linux equiv]; (2) `mgit sandbox image install` to fetch+verify+register a shipped image; (3) release pipeline builds+publishes the images as pinned assets; (4) brew leaves the user one command (or zero) from a working sandbox; (5) live validation on both platforms from the shipped artifacts.

nodes.title: Run the SSH litmus inside a REAL libkrun microVM (host-in, reverse-tunnel-blocked, policy-permits)
nodes.description: The three-part SSH litmus passes today against the netstack gateway with a SIMULATED guest (a second netstack on the other end of a real unixgram socket). Separately, the joined spike booted a REAL libkrun microVM against that same gateway and enforced allow/deny. What has not been done is the two together: the litmus inside a real VM. Owner asked for this explicitly.
nodes.prompt:
GOAL: run the existing three-part litmus with a REAL libkrun microVM in place of the simulated guest.

The litmus (internal/sandboxd/backend/libkrun/ssh_litmus_test.go, already in the default test suite, un-gated) asserts:
 1. the guest runs an SSH server and the HOST completes a real SSH session into it (inbound usable; the SEC-09 one-way publish direction);
 2. the guest CANNOT open a reverse tunnel to an un-allowlisted relay (default-deny; the T3 exfiltration claim);
 3. the SAME tunnel works once policy allows the relay (proving 2 is policy, not broken networking).

WHAT ALREADY EXISTS (do not rebuild):
- netGateway (netgw.go): netstack + tcp.NewForwarder + egress authorizer, DNS at gatewayIP:53, DialGuestPort for the inbound direction.
- The joined spike proving a real libkrun VM drives this gateway over libkrun's OWN unixgram socket, with allow/deny enforced end to end. Preserved at ~/mgit-vz-cache/libkrun-netstack-spike/ (netstack-spike/joined + netstack-spike/guest, with a README and run instructions). NOTE: that path is outside the repo — copy what you need in rather than depending on it.

WHAT IS MISSING:
- An SSH server in the guest. Options: (a) a small Go SSH server built with golang.org/x/crypto/ssh (already an APPROVED dependency and already used by the litmus's guest-side server — this is the low-friction path, and cross-compiles static for linux/arm64 exactly like the existing netguest binary); or (b) a real sshd in the guest rootfs, which is heavier but tests the actual daemon users would run. Prefer (a) first; note honestly in the result which was used.
- Guest addressing. The spike guest self-configures eth0 via SIOCSIFADDR/SIOCADDRT ioctls because there is no DHCP server. Production wants either DHCP served from the gateway (netstack can) or a static ip= kernel cmdline. Pick one and record it. WATCH OUT: the guest also enumerates a dummy0 interface — selecting "the first non-lo interface" picks the WRONG one and yields "no route to host"; select eth0 explicitly.
- Gating. This test needs libkrun + the hypervisor entitlement, so it must be build-tagged (libkrun && cgo) and/or env-gated, and it MUST SKIP LOUDLY with the reason when it cannot run — never silently pass. Follow the existing convention (TestE2E_VZF_* / TestE2E_* in the firecracker and vzf backends).

ALSO VERIFY WHILE THERE (both were bugs the simulated litmus caught, and a real VM is the stronger check):
- the gateway address must be a /24 (gwPrefixLen), not the /32 that tcpip.Address.WithPrefix() returns — a /32 leaves the guest off-link and makes ALL host->guest connections unroutable, which would break SEC-09 publishing entirely;
- DialGuestPort must wait for the guest's first frame (peerReady) rather than dropping host-initiated frames into a void; confirm a real booted guest satisfies this promptly (it ARPs the gateway during NIC setup).

Refs: ADR-010, MGIT-61.6, MGIT-61.8 (the re-exec lifecycle this will eventually run under).
Constraints: never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo/CI/commits; no AI-attribution trailers.
nodes.acceptance: All three litmus assertions pass with a REAL libkrun microVM as the guest, on macOS/HVF and (once libkrun is buildable there) Linux/KVM; the test is build-tagged and/or env-gated and SKIPS LOUDLY with the reason when libkrun or the entitlement is absent; guest addressing is DHCP or static-cmdline rather than in-guest ioctls, with the choice recorded; the /24 prefix and the peerReady wait are confirmed against a real guest; results recorded in ADR-010.
