nodes.title: Reconcile the single-backend decision: revise ADR-010 + MGIT-61.6, plan firecracker/vzf retirement, re-scope Windows
nodes.description: The owner directed consolidation onto ONE VMM backend ("we cannot keep on maintaining both firecracker and libkrun") plus earlier Windows support. ADR-010 and MGIT-61.6 were written under the earlier ADDITIVE framing ("keep firecracker/vzf, do not delete") and now contradict that direction. Governing documents that contradict the current decision are worse than missing ones — they will mislead the next agent. This task reconciles them and sequences the consequences.
nodes.prompt:
Read first: the MGIT-61 epic annotation "STRATEGIC DIRECTION CHANGE — OWNER DECISION 2026-07-29", then docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md.

THE SITUATION. ADR-010's Decision section still says "Adopt libkrun as an ADDITIONAL model.SandboxManager backend ... not a replacement ... Keep firecracker/vzf as fallback", and MGIT-61.6's acceptance says "firecracker/vzf remain fully functional and selectable" with out-of-scope "Do NOT delete firecracker/vzf". Those were correct under the additive framing. They are NOT correct under the owner's consolidation directive.

THE ANALYSIS THAT DROVE THE DECISION (preserve it in the ADR, do not re-derive):
- firecracker is Linux/KVM ONLY, so it CANNOT be the single backend. Choosing firecracker = firecracker + vzf + hyperv (THREE VMM integrations) and TWO egress implementations (Linux iptables; something else for macOS).
- Choosing libkrun = libkrun (Linux KVM + macOS HVF) + hyperv (Windows) = TWO integrations and ONE egress implementation.
- Neither covers Windows. Hyper-V stays separate either way and is today a 71-line stub (internal/sandboxd/backend/hyperv).
- libkrun additionally deletes every kernel we build (including the custom arm64 vz kernel, the heaviest artifact of the MGIT-61 milestone), the rootfs images, and the bundle-distribution pipeline; and the netstack gateway (MGIT-61.6, done) replaces a Linux-only ROOT-REQUIRING iptables engine with one portable rootless implementation that also serves Windows later.
- Costs accepted: CGO on Linux (the daemon is pure Go today), from-source libkrunfw on older distros (the Ubuntu 20.04 runner has no package), macOS 14+ floor (vzf supports 13+), and less-proven snapshot/restore — which matters if HyperSwe later wants warm-VM forking.

TASKS:
1. Revise ADR-010: Decision + Consequences to say CONSOLIDATE on libkrun, with the platform-count table and the accepted costs above. Keep the whole evidence trail (kill-tests, corrections, findings) intact — it is what makes the decision defensible.
2. Revise MGIT-61.6's acceptance + out-of-scope so they no longer mandate keeping firecracker/vzf.
3. Produce a SEQUENCED RETIREMENT PLAN as its own task(s): what must be true before firecracker/vzf, MGIT-30's kernel build, scripts/sandbox-image/publish.sh and the bundle install path can be removed. Do NOT delete anything until libkrun has (a) the re-exec lifecycle (MGIT-61.8), (b) the real-VM litmus green (MGIT-61.10), (c) mgit in the guest (MGIT-61.7), (d) Linux/KVM parity validated on the Linux runner, and (e) virtiofs perf measured on an npm-install-class workload. Retirement is the LAST step, not the first.
4. Re-scope Windows/Hyper-V (MGIT-12) against its new status as the ONLY other backend. Note that the netstack egress gateway is pure Go and portable, so Windows can reuse it — which is a significant simplification versus writing a third egress implementation.
5. Record the honest risk: consolidating means a single VMM dependency. The mitigation is that the microvm.Hypervisor seam stays intact, so a future backend is additive; say so explicitly rather than implying the risk is zero.

Constraints: keep ADR-010 local/untracked unless the owner says otherwise; no AI-attribution trailers.
nodes.acceptance: ADR-010's Decision/Consequences reflect consolidation on libkrun with the platform-count reasoning and the accepted costs, evidence trail preserved; MGIT-61.6's acceptance/out-of-scope no longer mandate retaining firecracker/vzf; a sequenced retirement plan exists as its own task with explicit preconditions and nothing deleted before they are met; MGIT-12 (Windows) is re-scoped as the only other backend, noting netstack reuse; the single-VMM-dependency risk and its mitigation are stated explicitly.

nodes.title: DECISION: publish the guest-image bundles now (unblocks HyperSwe pin) vs hold pending the libkrun consolidation
nodes.description: HyperSwe devs report the image bundles are built and waiting on a publish trigger; publishing completes HyperSwe's sandbox-setup pin. This is an OWNER-TRIGGERED, outward-facing action (no agent may run it), and it is a ONE-WAY DOOR that now conflicts with the consolidation decision recorded on MGIT-61: publishing commits mgit publicly to the kernel-distributor path that consolidating on libkrun is meant to retire, and creates a digest HyperSwe will pin against. There is also an unmet GPL precondition. This ticket forces the decision explicitly rather than letting it happen by default.
nodes.prompt:
DO NOT PUBLISH FROM AN AGENT SESSION. Release cuts and outward-facing publishes are owner-triggered. This ticket exists to surface the decision, its preconditions, and the cost of each branch — not to authorise the action.

THE REQUEST: HyperSwe devs report the multi-platform bundles are built and waiting on a trigger; publishing them completes HyperSwe's sandbox-setup pin (so `mgit sandbox image install` with no --from resolves from the latest release).

MECHANICS IF IT GOES AHEAD (docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md step 5):
  scripts/sandbox-image/publish.sh out/publish     # all platform bundles + checksums.txt
  gh release upload <tag> out/publish/*
  then verify on a CLEAN host: mgit sandbox image install && mgit run --sandbox -- echo ok
(The vz kernel build needs docker, so publish.sh must run on a machine that has it.)

WHY THIS IS NOT A ROUTINE STEP ANY MORE — THREE CONFLICTS:

1. IT CONTRADICTS THE CONSOLIDATION DECISION. See the MGIT-61 annotation "STRATEGIC DIRECTION CHANGE" and ADR-010. Consolidating on libkrun deletes MGIT-30's kernel build, the rootfs images, publish.sh and the bundle install path — libkrun brings its own kernel via libkrunfw and shares a virtiofs root. Publishing now makes mgit a public kernel distributor for artifacts we plan to retire, and gives HyperSwe a pin against them.

2. UNMET GPL PRECONDITION (flagged earlier, still open). The published bundle RE-HOSTS a Linux kernel binary (vendored from firecracker-ci) and a busybox-based rootfs. Both are GPL-2.0. Re-hosting makes US the distributor, so GPL §3 requires we make the CORRESPONDING SOURCE available, plus license notices, for the kernel AND busybox. Under libkrun that burden moves to upstream (libkrunfw publishes its source); today it is ours and it is NOT yet satisfied. This must be resolved BEFORE any public publish, independent of the consolidation question.

3. THE PIN IS THE POINT. Once HyperSwe pins a published digest, retiring the bundle path becomes a coordinated migration rather than a deletion. That is a real cost to pay knowingly, not by accident.

HYPERSWE IS NOT ACTUALLY BLOCKED — CHECK THIS FIRST. Development does not need the published bundle. A local install works today and is the same runtime:
  mgit sandbox image install --from <local bundle dir>
A validated darwin/arm64 bundle already exists at ~/mgit-vz-cache/bundle (kernel + rootfs + manifest.json), and publish.sh produces the multi-platform layout locally. Confirm with the HyperSwe devs whether their blocker is genuinely "we need a PUBLISHED artifact to pin" or just "we need a working sandbox" — those have very different answers.

THE DECISION TO MAKE (owner):
  A. PUBLISH NOW — accept the GPL obligations (satisfy them first), accept that HyperSwe pins something we intend to retire, and accept the migration cost later. Justified if HyperSwe genuinely needs a published, pinned artifact and cannot wait for the libkrun path.
  B. HOLD — keep HyperSwe on local bundle installs until the consolidation resolves (MGIT-61.8 lifecycle, 61.10 real-VM litmus, 61.7 mgit-in-guest, Linux/KVM parity, virtiofs perf), then publish whatever the libkrun path actually needs. Avoids distributing artifacts with a planned end-of-life and defers the GPL burden to upstream.
  C. PUBLISH AS EXPLICITLY PROVISIONAL — publish, but mark the bundle in release notes as a development pin with a stated end-of-life, so the later migration is expected rather than a surprise.

WHICHEVER IS CHOSEN: record it here and reconcile ADR-010 + docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md so the next agent is not left with contradictory guidance. If A or C, satisfy the GPL corresponding-source + notices requirement first and record how.

Refs: MGIT-61.2 (bundle publish mechanics), MGIT-61.11 (consolidation reconciliation), ADR-010, docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md
nodes.acceptance: The owner has recorded decision A, B or C on this ticket with reasoning; if publishing, the GPL corresponding-source + license notices for the re-hosted Linux kernel and busybox are satisfied and the method recorded, the release notes state the bundle's status (provisional or supported), and a clean-host verification of `mgit sandbox image install` + `mgit run --sandbox` is done; ADR-010 and the release checklist are updated so they no longer contradict the chosen path; the HyperSwe devs' actual blocker (published-pin vs working-sandbox) is confirmed and answered.

nodes.title: Sequenced retirement of firecracker, vzf, MGIT-30's kernel build and the bundle distribution path
nodes.description: The owner directed consolidation onto libkrun (MGIT-61 epic annotation, 2026-07-29; ADR-010 Decision revised in MGIT-61.11). This task executes the removal — and ONLY after every precondition below is met. Retirement is the LAST step of the milestone, not a cleanup that can be pulled forward: deleting a working backend before its replacement is validated on both platforms would leave mgit with no sandbox at all on whichever platform turns out to be unfinished.
nodes.prompt:
Read FIRST: docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md (Decision + Consequences, revised 2026-07-29) and the MGIT-61 epic annotation "STRATEGIC DIRECTION CHANGE".

DO NOT START THIS TASK until ALL of these are true. Check each one and record the evidence on this ticket; if any is unmet, stop and say which.

 P1. MGIT-61.8 re-exec lifecycle + Hypervisor.CreateVM — DONE (commit c8c02b2).
 P2. MGIT-61.10 real-VM validation green — PARTIAL. Boot + none-mode + allowlist default-deny pass on macOS/HVF (commit 2f59d52). The host->guest leg does NOT pass: SEC-09 port publishing is unwired on libkrun (see P6).
 P3. MGIT-61.7 mgit CLI in the guest — DONE for the ext4 image (commit c0c571d). NOT done for the libkrun delivery, where the guest root is a shared host DIRECTORY: the mgit binary must be staged into that tree instead of installed into an image. Doing this is part of retirement, because it is what makes the ext4 path removable.
 P4. Linux/KVM parity validated on the Linux runner — NOT DONE. libkrun must be built from source there (Ubuntu 20.04 has no package). Until libkrun is proven on KVM, deleting firecracker would leave Linux with NO sandbox.
 P5. virtio-fs perf measured — DONE on macOS (ADR-010 Gate 2: 0.216 ms/file write, 4.0x host). The Linux/KVM figure is still owed and belongs with P4.
 P6. SEC-09 host->guest port publishing works on libkrun. Today netGateway.DialGuestPort lives in the VM CHILD process and the daemon holds no reference to it, so there is no host->guest path at all. The fix is krun_add_vsock_port2(..., listen=true) — libkrun listens on a host unix socket and forwards into a guest vsock port, exactly firecracker's shape. Do NOT plumb the netstack gateway across processes.
 P7. SEC-03 quarantine DELIVERED on libkrun. CreateVM currently REFUSES any launch carrying a private store (fail-closed, correct as an interim) — which means the quarantined staged-worktree delivery is unimplemented. firecracker/vzf cannot be removed while libkrun cannot do the thing they do.
 P8. Gate 5 (macOS 14+ floor) accepted as a product decision, or vzf explicitly retained for macOS 13 — in which case this task is NOT a full vzf retirement and must say so.

THEN, IN THIS ORDER (each step independently revertable; do not batch):
 1. Flip the default: make libkrun the selected backend on Linux and macOS in cmd/mgit-sandboxd (today it is behind the "libkrun" build tag with !(libkrun && cgo) on the darwin/linux files). Decide whether libkrun stops being tag-gated at all — that is a release-packaging question (CGO in goreleaser, the libkrun runtime prerequisite, brew), so co-ordinate with the release checklist.
 2. Remove the firecracker backend + its e2e, then vzf + its e2e. Keep internal/sandboxd/backend/microvm untouched: it is the shared lifecycle and the seam a future backend plugs into. Watch for shared code that firecracker/vzf currently own — microvm.GuestMAC was already hoisted; check egress tap/iptables code (internal/sandboxd/egress/network_linux.go and the TapPlan machinery) which becomes dead with firecracker.
 3. Remove MGIT-30's kernel build (scripts/sandbox-image/build-kernel-vz.sh, fetch-kernel-fc.sh), the rootfs builders, build-bundle.sh and publish.sh, and internal/sandboxd/imageinstall + the bundle fetch/verify code — but ONLY after deciding what the libkrun deliverable IS (see below), because some of the signing/pinning machinery may be reused for it.
 4. Update every document that describes two/three backends: ADR-005, ADR-010, REQUIREMENTS FR-17.15, docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md, CLAUDE.md's sandbox section, README/CHANGELOG. A doc that still promises firecracker is worse than no doc.

THE DELIVERABLE QUESTION (answer before step 3): under libkrun there may be NO kernel and NO ext4 rootfs to distribute — libkrunfw brings the kernel and the guest root is a shared host directory. The artifact may reduce to a guest userspace TREE (which must contain the mgit CLI). Re-derive it from what the libkrun path actually needs; do not assume today's manifest.json/checksums.txt layout survives. This directly determines what MGIT-61.12 eventually hands to HyperSwe.

Constraints: never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo/CI/commits; no AI-attribution trailers; keep ADR-010 local/untracked unless the owner says otherwise.
nodes.acceptance: Every precondition P1–P8 is checked with evidence recorded on this ticket, and the task did not start until all were met (or the owner explicitly waived one, recorded here). nodes.title: GA-BLOCKING: libkrun networking is an opt-in build flag (NET=1) — detect it, document it, fail loudly
nodes.description: libkrun's krun_add_net_* symbols are behind an opt-in cargo feature; a default `make` build exports none of them while the shared header still declares them, so it fails at LINK time with a bare missing-symbol error. Because mgit requires an explicit NIC in every network mode (no NIC ⇒ libkrun enables TSI ⇒ full host egress leak), a default-built libkrun CANNOT host mgit at all. Today the macOS default path works only because the slp/krun tap happens to build with networking enabled — verified 2026-07-29 that brew's libkrun.dylib exports krun_add_net_unixgram — but that is an undocumented dependency on a third party's build flags, and it is documented nowhere in this repo (grep: zero hits).
nodes.prompt:
Found during MGIT-61 Linux/KVM parity work. Treat as GA-blocking distribution risk, not a footnote.

THE FACTS:
- libkrun gates krun_add_net_* behind an opt-in cargo feature. A default `make` produces a library WITHOUT those symbols, while include/libkrun.h still declares them — so the failure is at link time, naming a C symbol, which tells an operator nothing.
- mgit attaches an explicit NIC in EVERY mode (none/allowlist/open). That is a security requirement, not a feature: with no net device libkrun enables TSI and the guest gets full host egress (ADR-010, measured). So there is no degraded mode we could fall back to.
- Consequence: "install libkrun" is NOT a sufficient prerequisite. It must be a libkrun built with networking (upstream: `make NET=1`).
- macOS today works only because the slp/krun tap builds with it enabled. VERIFIED 2026-07-29: `nm -gU $(brew --prefix libkrun)/lib/libkrun.dylib | grep krun_add_net_unixgram` returns a match. If that tap ever ships a default build, `brew install hyper-swe/tap/mgit` breaks on every Mac.

WHAT TO BUILD (all three — each covers a different failure moment):
1. BUILD-TIME ASSERTION. Under -tags libkrun, fail the build with a message naming the cause and the fix, rather than emitting a raw undefined-symbol error. A cgo preamble check or a small link-probe in the Makefile target is enough. The message must say: libkrun was built without networking support; rebuild with NET=1 (or install a libkrun package that enables it).
2. RUNTIME CAPABILITY CHECK. mgit-sandboxd must verify at startup (or at first launch) that the linked libkrun can attach a net device, and refuse with an actionable error naming the remedy. Fail CLOSED — never fall back to a NIC-less VM, which is the TSI leak. Log which VMM and which capabilities were linked, alongside the existing startup log.
3. DOCUMENT IT. docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md prerequisites, the brew caveat, and the ADR-010 prerequisites section must all state that libkrun requires networking support, with the exact check a user can run.

ALSO:
- Inspect the slp/krun formula and record whether it passes NET=1 explicitly or relies on an upstream default. If it relies on a default, that is a supply-chain fragility for our macOS story — say so plainly in the ticket and consider whether the brew formula should assert the capability post-install.
- Add the capability check to the release checklist's clean-machine smoke step, so a tap change is caught before users hit it.

REQUIRED TESTS: the runtime check refuses fail-closed with the remedy in the message when the capability is absent (fake the probe — do not require an actually-broken libkrun); the startup log names the linked VMM and its capabilities; a doc test or grep asserting the prerequisite is present in INSTALL-SANDBOX.md.

Refs: ADR-010, MGIT-61.6 (the always-explicit-NIC guardrail), MGIT-61.8, docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md, docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md.
Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo.
nodes.acceptance: A libkrun built without networking fails at BUILD time with a message naming the cause and the fix, not a raw undefined-symbol error; mgit-sandboxd refuses fail-closed at runtime with an actionable remedy when the capability is absent, and never falls back to a NIC-less VM; the linked VMM and its capabilities are logged at startup; the prerequisite is documented in INSTALL-SANDBOX.md, the brew caveat and ADR-010; the slp/krun formula's reliance on NET=1 (explicit or default) is recorded; the release checklist's clean-machine smoke includes the capability check; required tests pass.

nodes.title: Sandbox starter: per-repo guest base an agent composes from OCI images
nodes.description: Ship a usable default guest base, and let a user's agent extend it into a per-repo "starter" carrying the tools that project needs (node, python, a compiler). Every sandbox created from that repo boots from the starter, read-only, with per-VM writable overlays. Under libkrun this is cheap because the guest root is a host DIRECTORY shared over virtiofs — a starter is just a tree, with no image build step. Owner decision 2026-07-29 (see MGIT-61.13): the sandbox targets the AGENT'S WORKLOAD, so the base must be able to run real toolchains.
nodes.prompt:
Read MGIT-61.13's owner-decision annotation first, then ADR-010.

GOAL: `.mgit/sandbox/base/` is a per-repo Linux userspace tree. All sandboxes for that repo mount it READ-ONLY; each VM gets its own overlay upper. mgit ships a usable default; the agent can compose a richer one.

TWO FOUNDATIONS ALREADY EXIST — reuse, do not rebuild:
- The guest already overlays a writable root over a read-only base, upper on a per-VM COW device (scripts/build-guest-image.sh:14-18). "Shared base, private writes" is already the model.
- images.lock already does per-repo digest-pinned, Ed25519-signed registration (internal/sandboxd/images). A starter MUST be registered the same way, so a base cannot be swapped silently under a task.

POPULATING IT — OCI is the mechanism. On macOS the agent cannot copy its own tools in (they are Mach-O); it needs Linux binaries. OCI images ARE Linux userspace trees:
    mgit sandbox base from node:22-slim
    mgit sandbox base from golang:1.24
Extract the layers into the base dir with go-containerregistry or oras-go — NO container runtime, no docker daemon. Benefits: the registry supplies digest pinning for free (feeds images.lock); the USER pulls the image, so mgit redistributes nothing and no GPL obligation arises; and every toolchain already exists as an image.

REQUIREMENTS:
1. Default base ships with mgit and works with no configuration (`mgit run` out of the box).
2. `mgit sandbox base from <oci-ref>` extracts to .mgit/sandbox/base/, records the resolved DIGEST, and signs the entry into images.lock. Re-running with the same ref is idempotent; a different digest is a visible change, never silent.
3. Also support "point it at a tree I built myself" — the escape hatch, and the GA-scoped path.
4. mgit + mgit-guest are INJECTED into the tree by us. mgit-guest MUST remain PID 1: a base image's own entrypoint/init is irrelevant and must never displace it. Assert this.
5. ARCHITECTURE CHECK: reject a base whose arch does not match the host's guest arch (linux/arm64 on Apple Silicon) with a clear error naming both — not a mystery boot failure.
6. libc COHERENCE: an alpine (musl) base with glibc toolchains breaks confusingly. Detect and warn, or refuse.
7. PROVENANCE — do this, it is a genuine audit win: record the base digest in the launch attestation, so a commit can say "produced in a sandbox built from base@sha256:...". Today we attest the commit but NOT the environment that produced it; this closes that gap. Refs: FR-17.6, ADR-002.
8. SEC-03 must be untouched: the base is read-only and is NOT the worktree; the staged worktree + private store delivery stays exactly as it is.

SECURITY NOTE — state this in the docs, because it reads backwards at first: letting users load arbitrary tooling into the guest is safe BECAUSE the guest is the untrusted side. That is what the VM boundary is for; a poisoned base burns a throwaway microVM. Everything that must stay protected (host store, egress policy, land airlock, attestation signing) is enforced HOST-side and is unaffected by the guest tree's contents.

TESTS: base registered + digest pinned + signed; re-pull idempotent, changed digest surfaces; arch mismatch refused with both arches named; mgit-guest is PID 1 even when the base image declares an entrypoint; base is read-only from the guest and per-VM writes do not leak between sandboxes; base digest appears in the attestation; existing SEC-03 hostile-guest tests still pass.

GA SPLIT: GA ships the default base + the bring-your-own-tree path. `from <oci-ref>` is a fast follow — do not put it on the GA critical path.

Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo; TDD per CLAUDE.md.
nodes.acceptance: A usable default base ships and works with no configuration; `mgit sandbox base from <oci-ref>` extracts layers without a container runtime, pins the resolved digest and signs it into images.lock, and is idempotent; a bring-your-own-tree path exists; arch mismatch and libc incoherence are refused or warned with clear messages; mgit-guest is PID 1 regardless of the base image's entrypoint; the base is read-only with per-VM overlay writes that do not leak across sandboxes; the base digest is recorded in the launch attestation; SEC-03 hostile-guest tests unchanged and passing.

nodes.description: Under MGIT-61. For `mgit sandbox image install` to work out of the box, the release must publish the guest images (kernel + rootfs) per backend as pinned, checksummed assets. Depends on the reproducible build (MGIT-30 + Linux equivalent). Linux/firecracker: a vmlinux + ext4 rootfs (mgit-guest PID1 + busybox); macOS/vzf: an arm64 vz kernel (built this session as 6.12.74 with virtio-PCI/BLK/CONSOLE/VSOCK/FS) + ext4 rootfs (busybox-musl arm64 + mgit-guest). Decide the vz-kernel story: reproducible build in the release job vs a vendored pinned kernel with a recorded provenance/digest (kernel.org rotates LTS tarballs off mirrors — pin the source or vendor the tarball; this is the MGIT-30 reproducibility concern made concrete). Keep the KVM box in scope for the Linux build/validate if hosted runners lack nested virt. Owner-triggered publish. Record each asset's sha256 in the manifest and in docs. nodes.title: Brew: leave the user one command from a working sandbox (caveat + docs for image install)

To make the sandbox active, the brew experience should leave the user at most one documented command from a working sandbox. Prefer a formula caveat that prints the exact `mgit sandbox image install` + platform prereqs (Linux KVM/firecracker; macOS 13+ arm64) rather than a 130MB image bundled in the formula (brew discourages large resources + network at install). Depends on MGIT-61.1 (install cmd) + MGIT-61.2 (published assets).

Keep it project-aware (do not touch mtix). Do NOT bundle the image in the formula. If a zero-command experience is later wanted, evaluate a separate cask for the image. nodes.title: FOLLOW-UP: distribution-trust — bake a HyperSwe release pubkey and verify published images against it
nodes.description: Under MGIT-61. v1 ships LOCAL-TRUST (image registered into the user's own trust root; distribution integrity = brew sha256 + GitHub HTTPS). This follow-up UPGRADES to distribution-trust: a HyperSwe release keypair whose PUBLIC key is baked into mgit, images signed by the release-held PRIVATE key at publish, and mgit verifies fetched images against the baked key in addition to (or instead of) the local trust root. Stronger provenance (survives a compromised release asset even if its sha256 is also swapped), but HARD TO REVERSE (the pubkey ships in every binary) and adds release private-key custody. Deferred until the owner wants it; requires a key-management decision.
nodes.prompt: Design + implement distribution-trust: decide key custody (where the release private key lives, rotation story), bake the release public key into mgit (embedded, versioned, rotatable), sign published guest images with the release key in the publish pipeline, and add a verification path so `mgit sandbox image install` trusts a distribution-signed image against the baked key. Keep local-trust working for user-built images. Document the threat model delta vs v1. This is a security-critical, owner-gated design — do not start without the key-management decision.
nodes.acceptance: Published images verify against a baked HyperSwe release pubkey; user-built local images still work; key rotation path documented; threat-model delta vs local-trust recorded.

nodes.title: Spike: evaluate libkrun as a cross-platform VMM backend (behind SelectBackend)
nodes.description: Time-boxed spike to decide whether libkrun (Apache-2.0, KVM on Linux + Hypervisor.framework on macOS/arm64, bundles its own kernel via libkrunfw, virtiofs root, virtio-vsock) can replace the bespoke kernel-build + rootfs + bundle-distribution path as mgit's primary VMM. Decision + license posture captured in docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md (local, unpublished). libkrun is added BEHIND internal/sandboxd/select.go (BackendFactories.Hypervisor) as an additional model.SandboxManager — NOT a replacement; firecracker/vzf stay as fallback and for snapshot/restore-class features.
nodes.prompt:
Read docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md first — it holds the full rationale, the license analysis, and the stability assessment. This spike proves (or refutes) that mgit's containment CONTRACT survives on libkrun before we commit to it.

libkrun is added behind sandboxd.SelectBackend as an additional model.SandboxManager implementation (BackendFactories.Hypervisor). Do NOT remove firecracker/vzf.

Clear ALL of these gates and record results on this task:
1. Link libkrun from mgit-sandboxd (CGO). Boot mgit-guest via krun_create_ctx/krun_set_root/krun_set_exec/krun_start_enter; vsock exec round-trips on BOTH Linux/KVM (the Linux runner) and macOS/HVF.
2. EGRESS: prove default-deny + allowlist (MGIT-11.7) holds under libkrun's TSI networking. TSI is userspace socket impersonation, not virtio-net — confirm our host-mediated egress model still enforces (none/allowlist/open round-trips).
3. virtiofs PERF: run a real npm-install-class workload (tens of thousands of small files); confirm acceptable latency for the agent loop.
4. LAND + SEC-03: the verified land airlock and store quarantine e2e pass unchanged on libkrun.
5. macOS floor: libkrun needs macOS 14+ (vzf path is 13+). Confirm acceptable or mitigate.
6. CHURN: N sequential per-task VM launch/teardown cycles with no leak/degradation (libkrun's proven pattern is one long-lived VM; ours is high-churn — this is the riskiest fit).

License guardrails (from ADR-010): link libkrunfw DYNAMICALLY; include Apache NOTICE + LGPL text; do NOT redistribute libkrunfw/busybox binaries ourselves — treat libkrun as a user-installed prerequisite like the firecracker binary. This keeps mgit Apache-2.0 with GPL strictly in the guest.

Output: pass/fail per gate with evidence, a go/no-go recommendation, and either (go) the migration/retirement plan for MGIT-30 + publish.sh + the bundle fetch/verify code, or (no-go) the fallback plan (OCI distribution + fetch-kernel-pinned-from-upstream). Do NOT run the MGIT-61 owner-gated publish while this is open — publishing commits us to the kernel-distributor path this spike may retire.

Constraints: never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo/CI/commits; no AI-attribution trailers in commits.
nodes.acceptance: All six gates in the prompt evaluated with pass/fail + evidence on both Linux/KVM and macOS/HVF; ADR-010 moved to Accepted (go) or Superseded/Rejected (no-go) with the decision recorded; a written go/no-go with the corresponding migration or fallback plan; no code path removes firecracker/vzf; license guardrails (dynamic-link libkrunfw, no self-redistribution of GPL binaries) honored. MGIT-61 publish remains un-run until this resolves.

nodes.title: Implement the libkrun hypervisor backend (mgit's single cross-platform microVM backend, behind the microvm.Hypervisor seam)
nodes.description:
Implement libkrun as mgit's microVM backend, carrying the spike's deferred gates (virtiofs perf, land+SEC-03 e2e, macOS floor, KVM/concurrent churn) as acceptance criteria. libkrun (Apache-2.0) gives one linked VMM across Linux/KVM + macOS/HVF and bundles its own guest kernel (libkrunfw), which retires the kernel build (MGIT-30), the rootfs image, the bespoke bundle distribution, and the external firecracker-binary requirement. Spike MGIT-61.5 returned GO: all existential kill-tests passed (API fit, real microVM boot on HVF, default-deny egress provable, 40/40 churn with no leak, ~120ms boot). Decision + evidence: docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md (Accepted).

SCOPE CORRECTION (owner decision 2026-07-29, see the MGIT-61 epic annotation): this is NO LONGER additive. mgit CONSOLIDATES on libkrun — firecracker and vzf are retired once the MGIT-61.11 preconditions are met. This task still does not DELETE them (retirement is sequenced separately and is the last step), but the acceptance no longer requires that they remain functional and selectable, and no design decision here should be shaped by preserving them.
nodes.prompt:
Read FIRST: docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md (rationale, license analysis, full spike evidence) and the MGIT-61.5 annotation (kill-test results + guardrails). Then internal/sandboxd/backend/microvm/manager.go and internal/sandboxd/backend/vzf/hypervisor_darwin.go — vzf is the closest analog to copy structure from.

## Architecture: implement the Hypervisor SEAM, not a new SandboxManager

A backend is NOT a full model.SandboxManager. The shared microvm.Manager already implements SandboxManager over a small per-platform seam. You implement:

  microvm.Hypervisor  — CreateVM(cfg VMConfig) (VM, error)
  microvm.VM          — Start(ctx), Stop(ctx, force)

and, as needed, the OPTIONAL seams the manager probes: GuestDialer (DialGuest — the vsock exec channel), GuestPortDialer (DialGuestPort — SEC-09 one-way publish), PeerIdentifier (PeerIdentity — host-observed, NEVER guest-asserted, SEC-05), NotifyListenerProvider (NotifySocketPath — guest->host land-ready auto-land trigger).

Consequence: SEC-03 quarantine, worktree staging, exec, land, attestation and notify logic are INHERITED from microvm.Manager + internal/sandboxd/staging. Do not reimplement them. Gate 4 is therefore mostly a matter of proving the inherited contract still holds on libkrun — not building it.

Package: internal/sandboxd/backend/libkrun/ (mirror vzf's file layout: hypervisor_<plat>.go, hypervisor_other.go, dialer.go, manager.go + _test.go peers).

## CRITICAL SECURITY GUARDRAIL (spike-proven, non-negotiable)

The spike empirically proved libkrun's DEFAULT LEAKS EGRESS: with no explicit net device, libkrun auto-enables TSI (Transparent Socket Impersonation), which proxies guest sockets through the host — the guest reached 1.1.1.1:443. Adding an explicit virtio-net device DISABLES TSI (same probe then returned "network is unreachable"). krun_add_vsock(ctx, 0) CANNOT retro-disable it (returns EEXIST; libkrun pre-creates its TSI vsock at ctx creation).

This collides head-on with the existing contract: VMConfig.AttachNIC == false currently means "attach no NIC" (none mode, FR-17.7). Under libkrun that is a FAIL-OPEN EGRESS LEAK.

Therefore, in the libkrun backend:
  - ALWAYS add an explicit net device (krun_add_net_unixgram/unixstream) in EVERY mode — none, allowlist and open.
  - AttachNIC == false / NetworkModeNone MUST map to "explicit net device wired to a deny/dead backend", NOT to "no net device".
  - If the net-device add fails, FAIL CLOSED — never proceed to krun_start_enter (proceeding would silently boot with TSI).
  - mgit's existing egress engine (internal/sandboxd/egress, MGIT-11.7) is the host backend that does allowlist filtering; allowlist/open route through it (gvproxy/passt-style unixgram/unixstream backend + guest DHCP/route).
This guardrail must be enforced structurally (in construction) AND covered by a regression test. A config path that can omit the net device is a defect, not a style issue.

## Packaging / platform constraints (spike-found)

  - libkrun dlopens libkrunfw.5.dylib BY LEAF NAME -> the daemon process needs DYLD_FALLBACK_LIBRARY_PATH (or an install-name/rpath fixup). mgit-sandboxd must arrange this; a missing libkrunfw must produce an ACTIONABLE error, not a bare -2.
  - macOS/HVF needs the com.apple.security.hypervisor entitlement — DISTINCT from vzf's com.apple.security.virtualization. Update build/darwin (+ release signing) accordingly.
  - libkrun requires macOS 14+ (vzf path is 13+). Gate 5 is a product decision: raise the floor or keep vzf for 13.
  - DO NOT BREAK THE DEFAULT BUILD. The Linux daemon is currently pure Go (no CGO); libkrun is CGO + a native lib. Put the backend behind a build tag (e.g. //go:build libkrun && cgo) with a hypervisor_other.go stub so `go install` / goreleaser keep working on hosts without libkrun. Verify: default `go build ./...` and `go test ./...` still pass on a machine with NO libkrun installed.
  - Ubuntu 20.04 (the Linux runner) has NO libkrun package — Linux validation needs a from-source libkrun + libkrunfw (a real kernel build). Budget for it; do not attempt it on a resource-constrained machine.
  - Add model.BackendLibkrun and register it in validBackends (internal/model/sandbox.go). Wire it into sandboxd.SelectBackend as a Hypervisor factory — it must NEVER be auto-selected as a silent downgrade, and must never displace firecracker/vzf.

## API shape (verified against libkrun 1.19.4 include/libkrun.h)

krun_create_ctx -> krun_set_vm_config(ctx, vcpus, ram_mib) -> krun_add_virtiofs(ctx, KRUN_FS_ROOT_TAG "/dev/root", rootdir) [+ a second virtiofs tag for the staged worktree at the identical path] -> krun_set_workdir -> krun_add_net_unixgram/unixstream(ctx, sock, fd, mac, features, flags) -> krun_add_vsock_port/vsock_port2(ctx, port, path, listen) -> krun_set_port_map (SEC-09) -> krun_set_rlimits (T7 caps) -> krun_set_exec(ctx, path, argv, envp) -> krun_start_enter (BLOCKS until guest shutdown; returns control cleanly — fits the VM.Start/Stop lifecycle).
Note the guest root is a HOST DIRECTORY shared over virtiofs, not an ext4 image — so the staging package's staged tree is shared directly. Confirm the staged-tree + private-store delivery (SEC-03) maps onto virtiofs tags correctly.

## SCENARIO-BASED TEST CASES (required; table-driven per CLAUDE.md)

A. Construction / unit (fake the krun layer; no VM boot; must run everywhere)
 1. TestLibkrunHypervisor_ConstructsFullConfiguration — VMConfig -> the expected krun call sequence/args (mirror TestVZHypervisor_ConstructsFullConfiguration).
 2. TestLibkrunHypervisor_BadImagePathsSurface — bad kernel/rootfs path surfaces, no partial VM.
 3. TestLibkrunHypervisor_NetworkNone_AttachesExplicitDenyNIC — THE guardrail regression: AttachNIC=false STILL adds an explicit net device bound to a deny backend. Fails if any path yields "no net device".
 4. TestLibkrunHypervisor_AllNetworkModes_AttachExplicitNIC — table over none|allowlist|open; every mode attaches an explicit NIC (no TSI fallback reachable).
 5. TestLibkrunHypervisor_NetDeviceAddFails_FailsClosedBeforeStart — krun_add_net_* error => VM never starts (no TSI-enabled boot).
 6. TestLibkrunHypervisor_RootfsReadOnly_Enforced — pinned image immutable (FR-17.17).
 7. TestLibkrunHypervisor_ResourceCaps_Applied — cpus/mem/rlimits reach the VM (T7).
 8. TestLibkrunHypervisor_PeerIdentity_HostObserved — identity is host-assigned, never guest-asserted (SEC-05/SEC-10).
 9. TestLibkrunHypervisor_WorktreeSharedAtIdenticalPath — virtiofs tag/mount yields the identical guest path (FR-17.3).
10. TestLibkrunLoader_MissingLibkrunfw_ReturnsActionableError — the leaf-name dlopen failure maps to a remediation message, not "-2".
11. TestLibkrunBackend_UnsupportedPlatform_Unavailable — no KVM / Intel mac / macOS<14 => unavailable, fail-closed (never a silent container downgrade).
12. TestSelectBackend_Libkrun_NotAutoDowngraded — selection wiring keeps FR-17.15 semantics.

B. Egress e2e (SECURITY — the spike's core finding; gate on libkrun present)
13. TestE2E_Libkrun_Network_None_NoEgress — mirrors firecracker's TestE2E_Network_None_NoEgress.
14. TestE2E_Libkrun_Network_Allowlist_ProxyAndDNSEnforced — allowlisted host reachable, off-list host refused, DNS enforced.
15. TestE2E_Libkrun_Network_Open_NATEgress — open mode reaches the network (and is audited as reduced control).
16. TestE2E_Libkrun_Network_TSIDisabled_NoImplicitEgress — the spike regression encoded: a guest that would have reached the internet under libkrun's default CANNOT under mgit's config. This is the test that would have caught the leak.

C. Containment / inherited contract (Gate 4)
17. TestE2E_Libkrun_Exec_RealGuest_RoundTrip
18. TestE2E_Libkrun_Land_RealGuest_RoundTrip
19. TestE2E_Libkrun_HostileGuest_SharedStoreUnreachable (SEC-03: host .mgit never reachable)
20. TestE2E_Libkrun_HostileGuest_EscapingSymlinkRejected
21. TestE2E_Libkrun_HostileGuest_LandIsOnlyBridge
22. TestE2E_Libkrun_PortPublish_OneWayOnly (SEC-09: host->guest only; no path back)

D. Churn / concurrency / perf (Gates 6 + 2)
23. TestE2E_Libkrun_Churn_SequentialLaunches_NoLeak — N launch/teardown cycles; no fd/process/mem growth, no latency drift. (Spike: 40/40, ~120ms, zero drift on HVF.)
24. TestE2E_Libkrun_Churn_ConcurrentLaunches_Isolated — M concurrent sandboxes; each sees ONLY its own staged worktree (cross-task contamination = T6).
25. TestE2E_Libkrun_Teardown_NoResidue — no leftover sockets/state dirs/processes after Stop+Remove (SEC-10 "no residue").
26. BenchmarkLibkrun_BootLatency + TestE2E_Libkrun_VirtiofsPerf_SmallFileWorkload — Gate 2: an npm-install-class workload (tens of thousands of small files) at acceptable latency. Record the number in the ADR; only hard-fail on a documented threshold.

E. Cross-platform parity
27. Run B/C/D on BOTH macOS/HVF and Linux/KVM (the Linux runner). Any gate that cannot run must SKIP loudly with the reason — never silently pass.

## Acceptance criteria

- libkrun backend implements microvm.Hypervisor (+ the optional seams it can honor) and passes A–E above on macOS/HVF and Linux/KVM.
- The egress guardrail is structural + regression-tested (tests 3, 4, 5, 16). No code path can boot a libkrun VM without an explicit host-controlled net device.
- firecracker/vzf remain fully functional and selectable; nothing is deleted in this task.
- Default (non-libkrun) build and test suite still pass on a host with NO libkrun installed (build-tag isolation verified).
- mgit-sandboxd resolves libkrunfw reliably; missing-lib and wrong-entitlement failures produce actionable errors.
- ADR-010 updated with the measured Gate 2 perf numbers, the Linux/KVM churn result, and the Gate 5 macOS-floor decision.
- Coverage per CLAUDE.md (store/service 95%, overall >=90% line); golangci-lint, go vet, -race, govulncheck all clean; anti-stub grep clean.
- License guardrails honored: link libkrunfw DYNAMICALLY; ship Apache NOTICE + LGPL-2.1 text; do NOT redistribute libkrunfw/busybox binaries — treat libkrun as a user-installed prerequisite (same posture as the firecracker binary today). Keeps mgit Apache-2.0 with GPL confined to the guest.

## Out of scope (do NOT do here)

- Do NOT delete firecracker/vzf, MGIT-30's kernel build, publish.sh, or the bundle install path. Retirement is a SEPARATE decision, taken only after this backend proves out in production use.
- Do NOT run the MGIT-61 owner-gated publish.
- OCI-based distribution is a separate follow-up (it addresses distribution; this task addresses the VMM).
- Snapshot/restore, GPU passthrough, nested virt: out of scope (and a reason firecracker stays first-class).

## Constraints

- Never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo, CI logs, or commits — call it "the Linux runner".
- No AI-attribution / Co-Authored-By trailers in commits.
- TDD per CLAUDE.md: failing test first, then implementation.
- This task is large and SHOULD be decomposed (suggested split: (a) seam + construction + guardrail unit tests, (b) vsock dialer + exec/land wiring, (c) egress/net backend integration, (d) packaging/entitlement/build-tag + platform gating, (e) churn/perf + cross-platform validation).
nodes.acceptance: libkrun backend implements microvm.Hypervisor behind a build tag; test groups A–E pass on macOS/HVF and Linux/KVM (or SKIP loudly with reason); the always-explicit-NIC egress guardrail is structural and regression-tested (tests 3/4/5/16); firecracker/vzf untouched and still selectable; default build+tests pass with NO libkrun installed; missing-libkrunfw and entitlement failures give actionable errors; ADR-010 updated with Gate 2 perf, Linux/KVM churn, and the Gate 5 macOS-floor decision; lint/vet/race/govulncheck/coverage per CLAUDE.md clean; libkrunfw linked dynamically with NOTICE+LGPL text and no self-redistribution of GPL binaries; MGIT-61 publish NOT run.

nodes.title: Ship the mgit CLI inside the sandbox guest image (agents cannot run mgit in the sandbox today)
nodes.description: The guest rootfs ships mgit-guest (PID-1 supervisor) + busybox only — NOT the mgit CLI. Since the agent's shell is routed into the microVM by `mgit run`, an agent inside the sandbox cannot run `mgit commit` / `mgit status` / `mgit log` at all. This also undercuts the SEC-03 design, which has the guest commit into a PRIVATE sandbox-local .mgit store that `land` then bridges to the host: nothing in the guest can write those commits. Verified 2026-07-29: scripts/sandbox-image/build-rootfs.sh installs only /sbin/mgit-guest + busybox, and cmd/mgit-guest is exec/land/notify plumbing with no commit capability.
nodes.prompt:
Verified gap (2026-07-29): the sandbox guest image does NOT contain the mgit CLI.

Evidence:
- scripts/sandbox-image/build-rootfs.sh (and the older scripts/build-guest-image.sh) install ONLY /sbin/mgit-guest plus the pinned busybox. No mgit binary.
- cmd/mgit-guest is exec/land/notify plumbing (serve_linux.go, bridge_linux.go, notify_linux.go) — it has no commit path.

Why this matters: `mgit run` routes the agent's shell INTO the microVM (see the sandbox section of CLAUDE.md: "Your shell commands run inside a hardware-isolated microVM"). So when an agent runs `mgit commit`, that command executes in the guest — where mgit does not exist. Worse, SEC-03's whole model is that the guest commits into a PRIVATE, sandbox-local .mgit store which `land` later bridges to the host shared store; with no mgit in the guest there is nothing to write those commits.

TASKS:
1. Add the mgit CLI to the guest rootfs build (build-rootfs.sh + build-guest-image.sh): CGO_ENABLED=0 GOOS=linux GOARCH=$ARCH, same reproducible flags already used for mgit-guest (-trimpath -buildvcs=false -ldflags=-buildid=), installed at /bin/mgit (or /usr/bin/mgit) and on the guest PATH. Keep the build reproducible — the rootfs digest is signed into images.lock.
2. Confirm which mgit subcommands must work in-guest (at minimum commit/status/log/diff against the private store) and which must NOT (anything that would reach the host shared store, or the sandbox/daemon control commands — those belong on the host). Make the host-only ones fail closed with a clear message rather than doing something surprising.
3. Verify the guest's mgit resolves the PRIVATE store at <worktree>/.mgit (the SEC-03 quarantined one), never a host store — add a hostile-guest test alongside the existing TestE2E_*_HostileGuest_SharedStoreUnreachable.
4. E2E: from inside a real sandbox, `mgit commit` a change, then land it, and assert the commit arrives in the host store with provenance. This is the loop the product claims and it is currently unexercised end to end from the guest side.
5. Size/impact: mgit is a much larger binary than mgit-guest; check the rootfs size increase against boot time (NFR-17.2) and the image-distribution size.

NOTE: if the libkrun direction lands (ADR-010), the guest root is shared over virtiofs rather than baked into an ext4 image, which makes this simpler — the mgit binary can be staged into the shared tree. Coordinate with MGIT-61.6.

Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo.
nodes.acceptance: The guest image contains a working mgit CLI on PATH, built reproducibly; an agent inside a real sandbox can run mgit commit/status/log against the SEC-03 private store; host-only subcommands fail closed with a clear message; a hostile-guest test proves the guest's mgit cannot reach the host shared store; an e2e proves commit-in-guest -> land -> commit present in the host store with provenance; rootfs size/boot-time impact measured and recorded.

nodes.title: libkrun VM lifecycle: re-exec child process per VM + Hypervisor.CreateVM
nodes.description: krun_start_enter never returns on success — it seizes stdin/stdout and exit()s the process with the guest's exit code when the VM shuts down. So mgit-sandboxd CANNOT run VMs in-process: the first guest to exit would kill the daemon and every other sandbox with it. libkrun needs a child process per VM, which is exactly firecracker's existing model. Owner explored and chose OPTION A: re-exec (the daemon spawns ITSELF with a hidden subcommand), not a second shipped binary.
nodes.prompt:
Read first: docs/adr/010-libkrun-backend-and-guest-distribution.md ("Implementation finding — libkrun is ONE VM PER PROCESS") and the MGIT-61.6 annotations. The pure-Go core (netBackingFor, newGuestCtx + NIC/host-peer invariant + AST pins, discardSocket, netGateway, the CGO binding) is DONE and lands unchanged inside the child — nothing there is wasted.

DESIGN (owner-chosen, Option A): mgit-sandboxd spawns ITSELF via os.Executable() with a hidden subcommand (e.g. `__krun-vm`); that child builds the libkrun context and calls krun_start_enter. Rationale: (a) no third binary to build/sign/ship/install/discover — the project's real distribution pain (MGIT-44 was "mgit-sandboxd missing from the archives"); (b) codesign applies to a BINARY PATH, so re-exec inherits the macOS entitlement by construction, whereas a separate helper needs its own goreleaser build id + post-hook and can arrive unsigned; (c) version skew is impossible. cmd/mgit-sandboxd/main.go currently does os.Exit(run(os.Args[1:], os.Stderr)) with a flag.FlagSet, so the hidden subcommand is an early branch in run().

TASKS:
1. Add VMConfig.StateDir to internal/sandboxd/backend/microvm (manager.go builds the state dir at ~line 294 and DROPS it; vzf works around it with filepath.Dir(cfg.OverlayPath)). libkrun boots a virtiofs root and may have NO overlay, so that trick yields "." — the deny/gateway sockets would land in the daemon cwd, be shared across sandboxes, and survive teardown's RemoveAll. This is a prerequisite, not a nicety.
2. Serializable VM spec crossing the process boundary (JSON on stdin preferred over argv — argv is world-readable via ps). The NIC + host-peer invariant must stay enforced IN THE CHILD; newGuestCtx is already the only constructor and is AST-pinned, so keep the child's main() a thin wrapper around it.
3. The child hosts its OWN netstack gateway / discard socket: its lifetime then matches the VM exactly and cleanup is automatic on exit. (Confirmed in the joined spike that Go goroutines keep running while krun_start_enter holds the process.)
4. Implement microvm.Hypervisor.CreateVM returning a VM that spawns/kills the child; Stop = SIGTERM then SIGKILL. NOTE: microvm.Manager.Launch does NOT call Stop when Start fails — the VM must self-clean, as fcVM.Start does.
5. Child stdio must be wired deliberately (pipes or /dev/null) — krun_start_enter SEIZES stdin/stdout, so inherited daemon streams would be handed to a hostile guest.
6. Exit-code semantics: the child's exit code IS the guest workload's exit code; libkrun reserves 125/126/127 for init failures. Distinguish "VM crashed" from "workload exited N".
7. vsock control plane across the boundary: libkrun's vsock ports are unix socket PATHS (krun_add_vsock_port) created by the child; the daemon connects to them — same shape as firecracker's per-VM vsock.sock, which is ALSO the SEC-10 peer identity. Reuse that pattern.
8. SelectBackend/platform wiring: a libkrun-tagged darwin build has two viable hypervisors and no tiebreak. Keep it GOOS+build-tag driven (platform_backend_libkrun.go under the tag; add !libkrun to the darwin/linux files) rather than adding a runtime BackendRequestLibkrun — a build-time fact must not enter the FR-17.15 runtime fail-closed contract. The daemon must LOG which VMM it linked at startup.
9. macOS entitlement: build/darwin/vz.entitlements currently has ONLY com.apple.security.virtualization. libkrun uses Hypervisor.framework and needs com.apple.security.hypervisor — a DIFFERENT key. Add both (one binary carries both backends) and verify the goreleaser post-hook signs it.
10. CI: nothing builds the tagged path today (ci.yml runs plain `go test ./... -race` with default tags), so binding_libkrun.go is compiled by nobody. Add a make target + a macos-14 job (brew tap slp/krun; brew install libkrun) or at minimum a -tags libkrun vet+lint step.

REQUIRED TESTS: child spawn/kill with a fake spawner (no real VM); Start-failure self-cleans (no orphan child, no leftover sockets); Stop force/graceful; stdio never inherited; exit-code mapping; concurrent launches isolated; teardown leaves no residue (SEC-10).

Constraints: never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo/CI/commits; no AI-attribution trailers; TDD per CLAUDE.md.
nodes.acceptance: VMConfig.StateDir added and used; mgit-sandboxd re-execs itself per VM via a hidden subcommand; the child builds the ctx through newGuestCtx (invariant + AST pins intact) and hosts its own netstack gateway/discard socket; Hypervisor.CreateVM returns a VM whose Start spawns and whose Stop signals the child; Start failure self-cleans with no orphan process or socket; child stdio never inherited from the daemon; exit codes distinguish VM failure from workload exit; SelectBackend wiring is GOOS+tag driven with the linked VMM logged at startup; darwin entitlements include com.apple.security.hypervisor and the release signing covers it; CI builds and lints the -tags libkrun path; required tests pass; lint/race/coverage per CLAUDE.md.

nodes.title: libkrun backend cleanup: reuse egress seams, open-mode authorizer, gateway logger, restore 95% coverage
nodes.description: Deferred findings from the /simplify passes over MGIT-61.6. None are defects in shipped behaviour; each is either duplication of an existing egress seam, a missing observability hook, or a gap the new code opened. Captured as a task because until now they existed only as prose inside MGIT-61.6 annotations.
nodes.prompt:
Cleanup backlog for internal/sandboxd/backend/libkrun (netgw.go, discard.go, ctx.go and their tests). Each item was raised by a /simplify review during MGIT-61.6, assessed as real, and deliberately deferred. Do them together — they are small and touch the same files.

1. REUSE THE EXISTING SPLICE HELPER. netgw.go handleForward hand-rolls the bidirectional io.Copy pair. internal/sandboxd/egress/proxy.go already has `splice` with the close-BOTH-sides-on-either-error discipline the local copy lacks. Export it as egress.Splice(a, b net.Conn) unchanged and call `go egress.Splice(guestConn, outbound)` (the `go` matters: handleForward must return promptly to release the forwarder's in-flight slot).

2. USE THE egress.DialFunc SEAM. netgw.go hardcodes (&net.Dialer{}).DialContext. egress.DialFunc exists (proxy.go), is injected by runner.go/supervisor.go explicitly "so the bound external interface is host-controlled", and is how dial faults get injected in tests. Add it as a bindNetGateway parameter; otherwise open-mode source binding diverges per backend.

3. OPEN MODE HAS NO AUTHORIZER. bindNetGateway REQUIRES a non-nil authorizer (correctly — a gateway with no policy is an open network), but egress/runner.go builds the per-sandbox assembly (Allowlist + Resolver + Audit + Authorizer) ONLY for allowlist mode, and keys it on firecracker's GatewayFor(). So nothing can construct an authorizer for open mode on libkrun. Add an allow-all authorizer in egress (a net GAIN: open mode would finally get per-flow audit records, which iptables NAT cannot produce), or an explicit open-mode branch. Also make the per-sandbox assembly constructible without firecracker's tap addressing so libkrun can reuse Runner.

4. NO LOGGER ON THE GATEWAY. netGateway swallows the authorizer error and the host-dial failure silently; egress/proxy.go logs the equivalent. Thread microvm.Config's injected *slog.Logger through (CLAUDE.md forbids package-level slog / global state). Same gap in discardSocket.drain(), which returns on ANY read error — if that ever fires for a non-close reason the guest's NIC is unserved and the VM hangs with nothing in the log.

5. EXTRACT THE DUPLICATED BIND PROLOGUE. bindNetGateway and bindDiscardSocket share an identical remove-stale / ListenUnixgram / Chmod triple and an identical Close-unlink tail, differing only in the noun in the error strings. Extract bindUnixgram(path, kind string) (*net.UnixConn, error) and removeSocketFile(path string) error in the same package; pass "deny socket" / "gateway socket" so the existing error-string assertions keep passing.

6. RESTORE COVERAGE TO THE 95% BAR. Currently 86.7% (it was 97.4% before the gateway landed). Uncovered: DialGuestPort's range-check and peer-wait timeout, serveDNS's bind-failure path, buildStack's CreateNIC/AddProtocolAddress failures, bindDiscardSocket's chmod failure. Add table-driven fail-closed cases.

7. TEST TIDYING. Fold TestNetGateway_AuthorizerError_IsTreatedAsDenial, TestNetGateway_HostDialFails_ResetsTheGuest and the off_allowlist_is_reset subtest into ONE table (they are the same shape: bind gw with authorizer A -> fakeGuest -> dial -> expect refusal). CLAUDE.md mandates table-driven. Also promote shortTempDir to internal/testutil.ShortTempDir — it is now the 4th copy of that pattern (sandboxd/daemon_test.go shortSocketPath, fcvsock, firecracker/dialer_test.go shortDir, plus ~9 inline os.MkdirTemp in the firecracker e2e tests).

8. PRE-EXISTING, ADJACENT: firecracker/paths.go derives vsock.sock (and reverseVsockSocketPath appends "_<port>") under an arbitrary stateDir with NO sun_path length check — the same failure mode libkrun now guards against in netBackingFor (bare "invalid argument" from bind(2)). Natural fix is hoisting libkrun's maxUnixSocketPath constant + check into microvm and calling it from both.

Constraints: TDD per CLAUDE.md; run /simplify after each small set; no AI-attribution trailers.
nodes.acceptance: egress.Splice reused (with its close-both discipline) instead of a local copy loop; bindNetGateway takes an egress.DialFunc; open mode has a constructible authorizer with per-flow audit; the gateway and the discard drain have an injected logger and no silent swallow; the duplicated unixgram bind/unlink prologue is extracted; libkrun package coverage back at or above 95%; the three refusal tests are one table; testutil.ShortTempDir extracted and used; lint/race/vet clean.

nodes.title: BUG: launching a sandbox for a never-squashed task fails "task branch not found" (first-use)
nodes.description: Found during the libkrun lifecycle work (MGIT-61.8). provision.Provision seeds the sandbox from the task branch tip, but task branches are created by `squash`, not by `commit`. So launching a sandbox for a task that has never been squashed fails with "branch not found: task branch task/<ID> in shared store". This is a FIRST-USE failure on the product's headline path — the natural order is work -> commit -> run in sandbox, and squash comes later. It was recorded only inside an MGIT-61.8 annotation; promoted to its own ticket because it is a user-facing defect independent of the libkrun work.
nodes.prompt:
REPRODUCE: create a worktree for a task, commit into it, then launch a sandbox for that task WITHOUT having run `mgit squash`. Expect: "branch not found: task branch task/<ID> in shared store".

ROOT CAUSE (directional — confirm it yourself before fixing, per the standing RCA rule): provision.Provision seeds the sandbox's private store from the task branch tip, but task branches are created by the squash path (see the squash semantics decision: squash produces a task-isolated artifact on task/<ID>), not by commit. A task that has been committed but never squashed therefore has no task/<ID> ref to seed from.

WHY IT MATTERS: this is the first thing a new user hits on the flagship flow. The documented order is `mgit work` -> commit -> `mgit run --sandbox`; squash is an integration step that comes later. Requiring a squash before a sandbox can launch inverts that. Per the owner's standing position, first-hour-user gaps are release-gating, not roadmap.

DECIDE THE CORRECT SEMANTICS (do not just make the error go away):
- Should provision seed from the task branch tip at all, or from the worktree's current HEAD / bound branch? Seeding from HEAD would match "sandbox the work I have now".
- If the task branch genuinely is the right source, should launch CREATE it (at the current tip) when absent, or should commit maintain it?
- Whatever is chosen must preserve SEC-03: the guest gets a PRIVATE store, never the host shared one, and the existing hostile-guest tests must still pass.

TESTS: an e2e that does work -> commit -> launch sandbox with NO squash and succeeds; a regression test for the exact error string so it cannot silently return; confirm the squash-first path still works.

Refs: MGIT-61.8 (where it was found), provision.Provision, the squash semantics decision, SEC-03.
Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; never put the Linux runner's LAN IP in the repo.
nodes.acceptance: A sandbox launches for a task that has been committed but never squashed; the chosen seeding semantics are documented with their rationale; SEC-03 quarantine and the hostile-guest tests still pass; an e2e covers work -> commit -> sandbox with no squash; the squash-first path is unregressed.

nodes.title: ADR + PLAN: extract the sandbox runtime into its own codebase (post-GA)
nodes.description: Owner proposal 2026-07-29: move the microVM sandbox into a separate codebase we also own, exposing one hardened entry point across Linux/macOS/Windows on amd64+arm64. mgit downloads it; responsibility for VMM, kernels, guest filesystem and their CVE/licensing burden lives there, leaving mgit a pure-Go VCS tool. Assessed as architecturally sound and cheaper than it looks — the seam already exists — but explicitly scheduled AFTER GA. Needs an ADR, not just a ticket, because it changes what mgit ships and introduces a cross-repo compatibility contract.
nodes.prompt:
Write ADR-011 and the extraction plan. DO NOT START THE EXTRACTION — this is post-GA by owner decision; splitting mid-refactor (re-exec lifecycle, netstack gateway, guest starter are all in flight) doubles coordination cost for zero user benefit.

## The proposal
A separate repo we own provides the microVM sandbox runtime as ONE hardened entry point across linux/macOS/Windows on amd64+arm64. mgit consumes it as an external dependency, the way it already consumes the `firecracker` binary today.

## Why it is viable (record this — it is what makes the cost low)
THE SEAM ALREADY EXISTS. mgit ↔ mgit-sandboxd is already a separate process with a documented wire protocol (IDD-FR17-SANDBOX-PROTOCOL.md). Extraction is a PACKAGING and OWNERSHIP change, not a redesign. The hard part — designing the boundary — is done.

## What it genuinely buys
- mgit becomes PURE GO on every platform again. CGO, libkrun, virtiofs, kernels all confined to the runtime. mgit's release becomes cross-compile-and-ship. Today CGO-in-the-release-path is the single largest untouched GA item.
- Two clocks, decoupled: kernel CVEs / VMM upgrades / guest refreshes run on a security cadence; mgit's VCS features run on a product cadence. Forcing them into one release is a large part of why this milestone dragged.
- ONE place owns the licensing posture (GPL notices, corresponding source, guest provenance) instead of it contaminating a VCS tool's release checklist.
- It matches the pattern already in use: `firecracker` is an external binary on PATH. This makes the external binary ours.
- The guest-starter work (MGIT-61.15) lands naturally in the runtime — guest userspace, OCI base composition and kernel are one domain. That the starter fits cleanly on the runtime side is evidence the proposed boundary is the right one.

## What it does NOT solve — state this plainly in the ADR
- The kernel/GPL/distribution burden RELOCATES AND CONCENTRATES; it does not disappear. If the runtime ships libkrun+libkrunfw so users get a one-command install, WE become the GPL kernel distributor — the exact liability the libkrun move was partly meant to avoid. That is arguably the right trade (one codebase solving it properly, with its own compliance process) but it must not be sold as elimination.
- Windows is unchanged. Hyper-V is still unwritten; it just gets written in the other repo.
- Two repos means two CIs, two release pipelines, two doc sets, and a compatibility matrix. For a small team that overhead is real.

## Two things that MUST be designed up front or the split goes wrong
1. VERSION COMPATIBILITY CONTRACT. Protocol version negotiation, a minimum-supported-runtime version, and a clear actionable message on mismatch. mgit already fails closed when the daemon is ABSENT; extend that to "present but incompatible". Version skew becomes a USER-VISIBLE failure mode the moment there are two artifacts.
2. THE POLICY BOUNDARY. The runtime owns VMM, kernel, guest filesystem, lifecycle. mgit owns worktrees, commits, land. But EGRESS POLICY IS SHARED — mgit decides the allowlist, the runtime enforces it. Draw that line explicitly, or the netstack gateway ends up half in each repo. Decide: does mgit pass a policy document the runtime enforces, or does the runtime call back to mgit per flow? (The former; the latter puts mgit on the hot path of every connection.)

## Deliverables
- docs/adr/011-sandbox-runtime-extraction.md with the above, an explicit "post-GA" status, and the boundary drawn as a diagram or table (which package/file goes where).
- A sequenced extraction plan as child tickets, with the version contract and policy boundary as the FIRST items, not afterthoughts.
- A statement of what mgit's release looks like after the split (pure Go, no CGO, runtime downloaded/installed how?) — including how a user without the runtime is told, and whether core mgit still works without it (it must: sandbox is FR-17, not the whole product).

Refs: ADR-005, ADR-010, IDD-FR17-SANDBOX-PROTOCOL.md, MGIT-61.15, MGIT-61.13.
Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; ADR-010 stays untracked; do not begin extraction before GA ships.
nodes.acceptance: ADR-011 exists with status post-GA, recording the rationale, what the split does NOT solve (relocated GPL burden, unchanged Windows, two-pipeline overhead), the version-compatibility contract, and the egress policy boundary decided explicitly; a sequenced extraction plan exists as child tickets with the contract and boundary first; the post-split release shape for mgit (pure Go, runtime as external dependency, behaviour when absent) is documented; no extraction work has begun.

nodes.title: Notarize the macOS artifacts (browser downloads are still Gatekeeper-killed; every other install path now works)
nodes.description: Verified on a second Mac 2026-07-31: extracting a release archive that was downloaded (AirDrop, so it carries com.apple.quarantine) yields binaries macOS KILLS on execution. `spctl -a -vv ./mgit-sandboxd` -> "rejected"; `./mgit --version` -> "zsh: killed" (SIGKILL, no dialog, no explanation). BOTH binaries are affected, not just the daemon. Cause: the release signs ad-hoc (codesign --sign -), and on Apple Silicon a quarantined ad-hoc-signed binary is refused by Gatekeeper. So every macOS user who downloads the release archive gets a product that dies instantly with a cryptic message.
nodes.prompt:
REPRODUCE (needs a SECOND Mac, or any transfer that sets the quarantine attribute — AirDrop does, scp does NOT):
  1. Build release archives (goreleaser).
  2. AirDrop mgit_<ver>_darwin_arm64.tar.gz to another Mac.
  3. tar -xzf ...; xattr -l mgit mgit-sandboxd   -> com.apple.quarantine present
  4. spctl -a -vv ./mgit-sandboxd                -> rejected
  5. ./mgit --version                            -> zsh: killed
  6. xattr -d com.apple.quarantine mgit mgit-sandboxd -> both run normally (confirms the binaries are fine; this is purely distribution/signing)

WHY IT WAS NEVER CAUGHT: `go install` builds locally (no quarantine) and Homebrew handles quarantine on install, so the ONLY affected path is a direct archive download — which nobody had ever exercised. Same pattern as every other defect this cycle: the failure lived exactly where nothing had been run.

CORRECT A MISLEADING COMMENT: .goreleaser.yaml's darwin signing hook says "Not a restricted entitlement, so no notarization is needed for it to be honored on Apple Silicon." That is true about the ENTITLEMENT being honored and says nothing about GATEKEEPER PERMITTING EXECUTION. Two different mechanisms. Fix the comment so the next person does not draw the same false conclusion.

OPTIONS (owner leaning: 3 + 2 now, 1 next release):
 1. NOTARIZE. Apple Developer account, notarytool + staple in release.yml, signing secrets in CI. The only fix that makes a plain download Just Work. Costs money and adds secret management.
 2. DOCUMENT the remedy: `xattr -d com.apple.quarantine mgit mgit-sandboxd` in docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md, the release notes, and the archive section of the README. Free and honest, but users who do not read it see only "killed".
 3. MAKE HOMEBREW THE SUPPORTED macOS PATH and mark the raw archive as advanced/at-your-own-risk. REQUIRES VERIFICATION FIRST — brew almost certainly strips quarantine, but that is currently an ASSUMPTION, and the brew formula is the surface that already shipped broken (it installed no mgit-sandboxd until this cycle).

TASKS:
 1. VERIFY the Homebrew path on a Mac that has never had mgit: brew tap hyper-swe/tap && brew install hyper-swe/tap/mgit, then run both binaries. If brew is also affected, options 2 and 3 collapse and notarization becomes mandatory for GA. This is the single most important unknown.
 2. Implement the chosen option(s). If 2/3: update INSTALL-SANDBOX, README, release notes, and the release checklist's post-publish smoke so the archive path is tested EVERY release, not once.
 3. Add a release-checklist step that downloads the published archive (not a local build) onto a machine that did not build it, and runs both binaries. A locally built or scp'd artifact does NOT reproduce this — the check must involve a real download or an explicitly set quarantine attribute.
 4. If notarizing later, record what it requires (account, cert type, notarytool invocation, stapling, CI secrets) so it is a scheduled decision rather than a surprise.

Refs: .goreleaser.yaml darwin hook, docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md, docs/release/RELEASE-CHECKLIST.md, MGIT-44 (the brew formula that shipped without mgit-sandboxd).
Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; ADR-010 stays untracked; never `git add -A`.
nodes.acceptance: The Homebrew install path is VERIFIED on a Mac that never had mgit, and the result recorded; the chosen mitigation is implemented (documented xattr remedy and/or notarization); INSTALL-SANDBOX, the README archive section and the release notes state the macOS download behaviour honestly; the release checklist gains a post-publish step that runs the PUBLISHED archive on a machine that did not build it; the misleading .goreleaser.yaml comment about notarization is corrected.

nodes.title: RELEASE BLOCKER: the first-run funnel is broken from an installed archive (no guest binaries packaged; base from needs a manual init)
nodes.description: Found on a second Mac 2026-07-31 with no mgit source checkout and no Go toolchain — i.e. a real user's machine. The documented first-run path fails twice, and the second failure means the OCI guest-base mechanism (the whole GA delivery story) does not work from an installed archive at all.
nodes.prompt:
Two defects in the same first-run funnel. Fix together and verify from an installed archive on a machine WITHOUT a source checkout — that constraint is the entire point; a scrubbed ENVIRONMENT inside the repo does not reproduce either bug.

DEFECT 1 — `mgit sandbox base from` requires a manual `image init` that nothing told the user about.
Observed:
  mgit work --sandbox        -> "Compose one from any Linux image: mgit sandbox base from debian:12"
  mgit sandbox base from ... -> "Error: ... read signing key (run GenerateTrustRoot first) ... (run `mgit sandbox image init` first)"
So the guidance we give leads straight into a second wall. Guidance that does not work is worse than no guidance.
FIX AT THE CLASS LEVEL: `mgit sandbox image install` ALREADY auto-creates the trust root when absent. `base from` (and `base set`) must do the same, rather than the error text being patched. Sibling commands should not differ on this.

DEFECT 2 — THE ARCHIVE DOES NOT SHIP THE GUEST BINARIES, so `base from` cannot compose anything.
Observed on the clean Mac:
  Error: guest base: build ./cmd/mgit-guest for the guest: exit status 1: go: cannot find main module...
  "The guest needs LINUX builds of mgit and mgit-guest, which a host install does not carry on PATH ... and which this install does not ship beside it either."
ROOT CAUSE, confirmed by reading .goreleaser.yaml: the `archives.ids` list is
  ids: [mgit, mgit-sandboxd-linux, mgit-sandboxd-darwin]
and does NOT include the guest builds. The builds themselves DO exist (dist/mgit-guest_linux_amd64_v1, dist/mgit-guest_linux_arm64_v8.0) plus the linux `mgit` builds — they are simply never packaged. So the binaries were added to `builds:` and never to `archives:`.
FIX: add the guest builds to the archive (they must land at a stable location the resolver looks for — `guest/mgit` and `guest/mgit-guest` beside the host binary, per the design), for BOTH linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, in the darwin AND linux archives. Then make the resolver's lookup order explicit and tested: --guest-bin-dir > archive-relative guest/ > source checkout. The source-checkout fallback must be LAST and must never be the thing that makes a test pass.
Also fix the stale help text on --guest-bin-dir, which says it "defaults to building them from an mgit source checkout" — that must not be the default for an installed user.

WHY BOTH WERE MISSED — read this before writing the verification:
A prior session reported "Verified by building real snapshot archives: the darwin/arm64 archive carries ELF 64-bit LSB, ARM aarch64." That verification inspected the dist/ BUILD DIRECTORIES (which do contain Linux ELF binaries) rather than the TARBALL. And its first-run test ran with a scrubbed environment but from a working directory where `go build ./cmd/mgit-guest` still succeeded, so the source-checkout fallback silently rescued it and the archive-relative lookup was never exercised. Do not repeat either mistake.

REQUIRED VERIFICATION (all three):
 1. `tar -tzf` the actual archive and assert guest/mgit + guest/mgit-guest are present, for each archive that should carry them. Add this as an automated test — the existing goreleaser assertion test is the natural home.
 2. Extract the archive into a directory that is NOT inside any Go module and has no Go toolchain on PATH, then run the full funnel: image init (or nothing, if defect 1 is fixed) -> base from debian:12 -> work --sandbox -> mgit run. It must work end to end.
 3. A test that fails if the resolver falls back to source-building when archive-relative binaries are present.

Refs: MGIT-61.15, MGIT-64 (the Gatekeeper quarantine blocker found in the same session), .goreleaser.yaml archives.ids, docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md.
Constraints: no AI-attribution trailers; ADR-010 stays untracked; never `git add -A`; do not publish, push tags, or merge to main.
nodes.acceptance: `mgit sandbox base from`/`base set` create the trust root automatically like `image install` does; the release archives contain guest/mgit and guest/mgit-guest for linux/arm64 and linux/amd64, asserted by an automated test against the actual tarball; the guest-binary resolver prefers --guest-bin-dir then archive-relative then source checkout, with a test proving it does not fall back to source-building when archive binaries exist; the --guest-bin-dir help text no longer claims source-building is the default; and the whole funnel (base from -> work --sandbox -> mgit run) is verified from an extracted archive outside any Go module with no Go toolchain available.

nodes.title: RELEASE BLOCKER: the Homebrew tap is PRIVATE, so the recommended install path fails for every external user
nodes.description: Verified 2026-07-31: hyper-swe/mgit is PUBLIC (200 unauthenticated) but hyper-swe/homebrew-tap is PRIVATE (404 unauthenticated). `brew tap hyper-swe/tap` therefore prompts for GitHub credentials and fails for anyone outside the org — while `brew install hyper-swe/tap/mgit` is presented as the RECOMMENDED install path in both the README and docs/INSTALL-SANDBOX.md. The product is public; its primary documented install channel is not. Discovered when a second Mac could not tap it; it also explains an earlier "No available formula ... Please tap it" that was misread as a stale machine.
nodes.prompt:
A repository-visibility problem, not a code defect — but it blocks the release, and it cascades.

VERIFY FIRST (do not assume it is still true):
  gh repo view hyper-swe/homebrew-tap --json isPrivate,visibility
  curl -s -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}\n' https://github.com/hyper-swe/homebrew-tap   # 404 = private/absent
  gh repo view hyper-swe/mgit --json isPrivate                                          # expected PUBLIC

THE FIX IS OWNER ACTION: make hyper-swe/homebrew-tap public. A tap holds Ruby formulae and nothing sensitive; being public is how brew works at all. Nobody but the owner can flip this.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND ITSELF:
- MGIT-64 (downloaded archives are SIGKILLed by Gatekeeper) proposed "make Homebrew the supported macOS path" as the mitigation. That is IMPOSSIBLE while the tap is private, so MGIT-64's chosen remedy depends on this.
- MGIT-64's key unknown — does brew strip com.apple.quarantine? — CANNOT BE TESTED until the tap is reachable.
- The release checklist's "reconcile the Homebrew tap" step assumes a tap users can reach.
